field.summary: Retention window for admin activity log entries; older ones are pruned.
field.usage: How long admin activity log entries are kept before cleanup removes them. The field note asks for a number of days; a shorter window keeps the log table small, a longer one preserves more audit history for investigations.

field.summary: Turns admin activity logging on or off.
field.usage: When Yes, actions performed by admin users are recorded to the admin activity log. Set to No to stop collecting this log.

field.summary: Whether admin login activity is recorded.
field.usage: When Yes, admin user sign-in activity is captured in the admin activity log.

field.summary: Whether admin page visits are recorded.
field.usage: When Yes, the admin pages visited by admin users are captured in the admin activity log.

field.summary: Whether admin CAPTCHA answers must match letter case.
field.usage: When Yes, the entered CAPTCHA text must match the case of the displayed characters. Applies only when Enable CAPTCHA in Admin is set to Yes.

field.summary: Turns the built-in image CAPTCHA on or off for Admin Panel forms.
field.usage: When Yes, the legacy image CAPTCHA is required on the selected admin forms; No disables it. Applies to the Admin Panel.

field.summary: Failed-login threshold before the admin CAPTCHA appears; 0 means it is always shown.
field.usage: Number of failed admin logins allowed before CAPTCHA is required. Applies only when admin CAPTCHA is enabled and set to show after failures. Lower values block brute-force attempts sooner; as the native note says, 0 shows CAPTCHA on every login attempt.

field.summary: The font used to render the admin CAPTCHA image.
field.usage: Selects which configured font the CAPTCHA characters are drawn with. Applies only when Enable CAPTCHA in Admin is set to Yes.

field.summary: Which Admin Panel forms display the CAPTCHA.
field.usage: Selects the admin forms (such as login and forgot password) that require a CAPTCHA. Applies only when Enable CAPTCHA in Admin is set to Yes.

field.summary: Number of CAPTCHA characters (max 8, range allowed); higher is harder for bots and humans.
field.usage: How many characters the CAPTCHA challenge shows (8 max; a range like 3-5 randomises the count). More characters make it harder for bots but also for people. Applies only when CAPTCHA is enabled.

field.summary: When the admin CAPTCHA is shown — e.g. always or after failed attempts.
field.usage: Chooses when a CAPTCHA is required, such as always or only after a number of failed login attempts. Applies only when Enable CAPTCHA in Admin is set to Yes.

field.summary: The character pool CAPTCHA images are drawn from; applies only when CAPTCHA is enabled.
field.usage: Defines which characters can appear in generated CAPTCHA images. The field note restricts this to letters and digits and warns that look-alike characters lower recognition. Applies only when admin CAPTCHA is enabled.

field.summary: How many minutes a displayed admin CAPTCHA stays valid before expiring.
field.usage: The lifetime, in minutes, of a displayed CAPTCHA before a new one must be generated. Applies only when Enable CAPTCHA in Admin is set to Yes.

field.summary: Whether charts are displayed on the Admin dashboard.
field.usage: When Yes, the Admin dashboard renders its sales/order charts. Disabling can reduce load on large stores where the chart queries are heavy.

field.summary: Which store email identity sends Admin password forgot/reset emails.
field.usage: The sender identity for Admin 'forgot password' and reset emails — one of the Store Email Addresses identities (General Contact, Sales Representative, Customer Support, Custom 1/2).

field.summary: Template used for the admin forgot-password email.
field.usage: The email template sent when an admin user requests a password reset. As the field note says, the Default option resolves through theme fallback; pick a custom template to override the wording or branding of that message.

field.summary: Email template for notifying a newly created admin user.
field.usage: The template for the email sent to a newly created admin user. As the native note says, Default follows theme fallback. Global scope.

field.summary: Template for admin-user notification emails; pick a custom one to override the theme default.
field.usage: Selects the email template for admin user notification messages. A custom template overrides the theme default, which is used when 'Default' is selected.

field.summary: Caps the product count loaded into the admin grid to speed it up on large catalogs.
field.usage: When Yes, limits how many products the admin grid collection loads. On large catalogs this noticeably speeds up the grid, but reported totals and some filtering become approximate. When No, the full count is used. Global scope.

field.summary: Caps products loaded in the admin grid to keep large catalogs responsive (minimum 20000).
field.usage: Caps how many products the admin product grid loads so very large catalogs stay responsive; the minimum is 20000. Applies only when limiting the total number of products in the grid is enabled.

field.summary: No blocks concurrent logins to one admin account (more secure); Yes allows the same account from multiple machines.
field.usage: When No (the safer default, per the note), a new login elsewhere ends the existing session, so an admin account can't be used from two machines at once. Yes permits concurrent sessions — needed only when a team genuinely shares one login. Default scope.

field.summary: Failed admin logins before lockout; lower is safer but risks locking out admins, empty disables it.
field.usage: How many consecutive failed admin logins trigger an account lockout. A lower number hardens against brute-force attempts but risks locking out legitimate admins; leaving it empty disables lockout entirely.

field.summary: How long, in minutes, an admin account stays locked after too many failed logins.
field.usage: The duration, in minutes, that an admin account is locked once the failed-login limit is reached, after which sign-in is allowed again.

field.summary: Caps admin password-reset requests per hour to curb abuse; 0 disables the limit. Tied to the chosen reset-protection type.
field.usage: Limits how many admin password-reset requests are accepted per hour, throttling abuse and denial-of-service attempts (native note). Set 0 to disable the cap. Applies under the selected password reset protection type (depends). Global setting (default scope).

field.summary: Throttles repeated admin password-reset requests to curb abuse; 0 disables the delay.
field.usage: Minimum delay, in minutes, between successive password-reset requests, limiting abuse and email flooding. Use 0 to disable. Applies only under the matching password-reset protection type.

field.summary: Shortest allowed admin password; longer minimums resist brute-force guessing. The enforced floor is 7 characters.
field.usage: Sets the minimum character count for admin passwords, applied whenever one is set or changed. Longer minimums make admin accounts harder to brute-force. The native note states values below 7 are rejected. Global setting (default scope).

field.summary: Whether a periodic admin password change is forced or only recommended.
field.usage: Chooses whether admins are required to change their password once the password lifetime elapses, or merely prompted to. Governs how the password-expiry policy is applied.

field.summary: Days before an admin password must be changed; leave empty to disable expiry.
field.usage: The number of days an admin password stays valid before the user must change it. As the field note says, leaving the field empty disables password expiry entirely, so admins are never forced to rotate.

field.summary: Hours an admin password-recovery link stays valid; shorter limits the window a leaked link can be used.
field.usage: How many hours an admin password-reset link remains usable before it expires (enter 1 or more, per the note). Shorter periods reduce the window in which an intercepted or forwarded recovery link could reset an admin password. Default scope.

field.summary: How admin password-reset requests are rate-limited — by IP, email, both, or not at all.
field.usage: Limits admin forgot-password requests by By IP and Email, By IP, By Email, or None, to throttle abuse of the password-reset flow.

field.summary: How long an idle admin stays signed in; shorter is safer but logs admins out more often.
field.usage: Idle time, in seconds, before an admin session expires and the user must log in again. Shorter values limit the risk of unattended sessions; longer values are more convenient but less secure. Must be between 60 and 31536000 (one year).

field.summary: Whether Admin usernames are matched case-sensitively at login.
field.usage: When Yes, Admin login treats the username as case-sensitive; when No, case is ignored.

field.summary: Adds a secret key to Admin URLs to protect against cross-site request forgery.
field.usage: When Yes, Admin URLs include a per-session secret key, a CSRF protection. Leave enabled unless a specific integration requires otherwise.

field.summary: The Admin page shown first after a user signs in.
field.usage: The landing page displayed when an Admin user logs in, chosen from the available Admin menu destinations.

field.summary: Selects which installed theme is used for the Admin panel interface.
field.usage: Chooses the active Admin theme from the themes installed for the backend, changing the look of the Admin panel.

field.summary: Overrides the admin host/URL; a wrong value can lock you out of admin, and it takes effect only after a cache flush.
field.usage: Replaces the base URL used for the admin panel (applies only when Use Custom Admin URL is enabled). It must end in a slash and point at a URL that actually serves Magento, since a wrong value locks you out of admin. The change takes effect after the configuration cache is flushed.

field.summary: Replaces the default /admin path with a custom one; you are signed out and must re-login after saving.
field.usage: Changes the admin panel's URL path for obscurity, so the panel no longer answers at the default address. Applies only when 'Use Custom Admin Path' is enabled. After saving you are logged out and must sign in at the new path, and old bookmarks break.

field.summary: Whether the Admin panel is served from a custom base URL.
field.usage: When Yes, the Admin uses a custom base URL instead of the default. Set the URL in the related field. Misconfiguration can lock you out of the Admin.

field.summary: Whether the Admin is reached at a custom path instead of the default.
field.usage: When Yes, the Admin is accessed under a custom path (e.g. /myadmin) rather than the default. Set the path in the related field. Misconfiguration can lock you out of the Admin.

field.summary: Sends anonymized admin-UI usage telemetry to Magento; turn off if your data-privacy policy forbids outbound tracking.
field.usage: Beyond opting into usage tracking, this streams anonymized data about how admins use the panel back to Magento/Adobe. Turn it off (No) where your data-privacy policy forbids outbound telemetry. It affects neither the storefront nor store performance.

field.summary: Scheduled retranslation overwrites manual product-translation edits on the next cron run; can differ per store view.
field.usage: The native note warns it overwrites manual edits. The mechanism: retranslation runs on a schedule via cron, so any hand-corrected product translation is replaced the next time the job runs. Leave it No if editors maintain translations by hand. Scoped per website/store view.

field.summary: Set to No to skip URL rewrite generation during automatic translation and save performance; translated URLs then need rebuilding separately.
field.usage: Yes/No. Controls whether URL rewrites are generated for translated URLs during automatic translation. Setting No saves processing time, but newly translated-language URLs stay unbrowsable until you regenerate the rewrites by another means. Can be set per website and store view.

field.summary: How often product translations are processed; too frequent adds API load, too rare delays new translations.
field.usage: Schedule, in Unix crontab syntax, for the batch job that translates product data. Tighter intervals pick up changes sooner but add translation-API calls and server load; wider intervals save cost but delay new translations. The expression is validated before saving.

field.summary: Days before an already-translated product is retranslated; lower means more frequent, costlier re-runs.
field.usage: Sets how stale a translation may get before periodic retranslation redoes it, measured from each product's Last translation date. A shorter period keeps catalog copy fresher but triggers more translation-engine calls and cost. Applies only when periodic retranslation is enabled; website/store scoped.

field.summary: Picks which select/multiselect product attributes get their options auto-translated; set per store view.
field.usage: Chooses the select and multiselect product attributes whose options are automatically translated. As the field note says, empty options are always translated and the auto-retranslation toggle below has no effect here. Scoped to default/website/store, so each store view can translate a different set.

field.summary: Schedules the background job that translates select-attribute values; uses standard cron syntax.
field.usage: Cron schedule for the job that translates dropdown/select attribute values. The native note gives the syntax. Running it too frequently can run up translation-API calls and cost, while infrequent runs leave new values untranslated longer. Global (default) scope only.

field.summary: More selected attributes means more content sent to the translation engine — higher cost and processing time.
field.usage: Each attribute you pick here is sent to the translation engine, so adding more raises translation volume, cost and processing time. Only text attributes are eligible. Set per website or store view, so different locales can translate different fields.

field.summary: Yes lets the scheduled auto-translation also process disabled products, spending translation credits on items not on the storefront.
field.usage: When Yes, the periodic automatic-translation run (not the manual button, per the note) also translates products that are disabled. Effect: translation-API calls and credits are spent on items that aren't visible on the storefront. Set per website or store view.

field.summary: Shows the language texts are translated into — the target store view's configured Locale.
field.usage: Read-only indicator of the automatic-translation target language. It follows the Locale of the target store view (General > Locale options), so change the language there rather than here. Differs per store view.

field.summary: Turns AI automatic translation on or off.
field.usage: When Yes, the AI Integration automatic translation feature is active. Can be set per website or store view, so translation can run on some stores and not others.

field.summary: The base language the AI translates from; set it wrong and every translation starts from the wrong source text.
field.usage: Tells the translation engine which language your product data is already written in, so it translates from the correct base. Set it to the wrong language and otherwise-correct content gets mistranslated. Applies store-wide.

field.summary: DeepL API key used for translations; stored encrypted and only used when DeepL is the engine.
field.usage: The DeepL authentication key the module uses to call the translation API; the field note links where to create one. It is stored encrypted at rest, and applies only when the translation engine is set to DeepL.

field.summary: Chooses the external translation service; each engine has its own quality, cost and API credentials.
field.usage: Sets which external service performs all automatic translation (DeepL, OpenAI, etc.). Switching it changes translation quality and cost, and requires that engine's own API credentials to be configured. Store-wide setting.

field.summary: Credential for the Gemini engine; stored encrypted. Without a valid key, Gemini translation calls fail.
field.usage: API key used to authenticate with Google Gemini, stored encrypted. Used only when the translation engine is set to Google Gemini. If it is missing or invalid, translation requests to Gemini fail.

field.summary: Picks the Google Gemini model used for translation; options load after a valid API key is saved.
field.usage: Which Gemini model performs translations. Applies only when the translation engine is set to Google Gemini. The choice trades translation quality against speed and API cost; the list appears once a valid API key is saved, per the native note. Global scope.

field.summary: Credential for the OpenAI translation engine; stored encrypted and used only when that engine is selected.
field.usage: Authenticates calls to OpenAI for automatic translation. Entered as an obscured field and stored encrypted, and only used when the translation engine is set to OpenAI. Set at default scope — a single key serves all stores.

field.summary: Picks the OpenAI model used for translation; higher-tier models cost more per request and differ in quality and speed.
field.usage: Chooses which OpenAI model performs the translations. Options appear only after a valid API key and organization ID are saved. The choice trades translation quality against per-request cost and speed — see the linked OpenAI docs. Applies only when the OpenAI engine is selected.

field.summary: Only needed if your OpenAI account spans multiple organizations; used only when the OpenAI translation engine is selected.
field.usage: Set this only if your OpenAI account belongs to more than one organization and requests must be scoped/billed to a specific one; otherwise leave it blank to use your default org. Applies only when the OpenAI translation engine is selected.

field.summary: Scopes OpenAI usage and billing to one project; stored encrypted. Only used when the OpenAI translation engine is selected.
field.usage: The OpenAI project this store's translation calls are billed and tracked against; stored encrypted. Applies only when the translation engine is set to OpenAI. Left blank, OpenAI uses your default project (per the note), so set it to isolate spend or usage limits per project.

field.summary: Your DHL account number.
field.usage: The DHL account used for rating and shipping.

field.summary: Offer live DHL rates at checkout.
field.usage: When Yes, DHL shipping rates are requested and offered to customers.

field.summary: Your DHL REST API key.
field.usage: Credential for the DHL REST API.

field.summary: Your DHL REST API secret.
field.usage: Credential paired with the API key for the DHL REST API.

field.summary: Whether shipments are documents or goods.
field.usage: Classifies DHL shipments as documents or non-document goods, which changes the services available.

field.summary: Log DHL API requests and responses.
field.usage: When Yes, DHL API traffic is written to the debug log for troubleshooting.

field.summary: Default package depth sent to DHL.
field.usage: The package depth used in DHL rate requests when specific dimensions are enabled.

field.summary: Split heavy orders into multiple packages.
field.usage: When Yes, orders over DHL's weight limit are divided into several packages for rating.

field.summary: DHL document services offered.
field.usage: The DHL services available for document shipments.

field.summary: DHL document service used for free shipping.
field.usage: The document service applied when an order qualifies for free shipping.

field.summary: DHL non-document service used for free shipping.
field.usage: The goods service applied when an order qualifies for free shipping.

field.summary: Offer free DHL shipping above a subtotal.
field.usage: When enabled, DHL shipping is free once the order meets the subtotal below.

field.summary: Order subtotal that qualifies for free DHL shipping.
field.usage: Orders at or above this subtotal ship free via the chosen DHL free method.

field.summary: Whether DHL handling applies per order or per package.
field.usage: Whether the handling fee is charged once per order or for each package.

field.summary: A handling fee added to DHL rates.
field.usage: An extra amount added on top of DHL's returned rate.

field.summary: Whether the DHL handling fee is fixed or a percentage.
field.usage: Whether the handling fee is a fixed amount or a percentage of the rate.

field.summary: Default package height sent to DHL.
field.usage: The package height used in DHL rate requests when specific dimensions are enabled.

field.summary: Your DHL API site/user ID.
field.usage: Credential identifying your account to the DHL API.

field.summary: DHL non-document services offered.
field.usage: The DHL services available for non-document (goods) shipments.

field.summary: Your DHL API password.
field.usage: Credential used to authenticate to the DHL API.

field.summary: Hours until the shipment is ready for pickup.
field.usage: How long after an order DHL should expect the package to be ready.

field.summary: Whether DHL is limited to specific countries.
field.usage: Offer DHL in all allowed countries, or restrict it to the countries chosen below.

field.summary: Use the DHL test environment.
field.usage: When Yes, requests go to DHL's sandbox instead of production.

field.summary: Show DHL even when it returns no rates.
field.usage: When Yes, DHL is shown (with its error message) instead of being hidden when it can't return rates.

field.summary: Whether to send specific package dimensions.
field.usage: Whether DHL rates use a regular package or the specific height/width/depth entered above.

field.summary: Position of DHL among shipping methods.
field.usage: Controls where DHL appears in the list of shipping options. Lower numbers appear first.

field.summary: The countries DHL ships to.
field.usage: The countries where DHL is offered, used when it is limited to specific countries.

field.summary: Message shown when DHL is unavailable.
field.usage: The text shown to customers when DHL can't return a rate.

field.summary: The carrier heading shown for DHL.
field.usage: The group title shown above DHL's rates at checkout.

field.summary: Which DHL API to use.
field.usage: Whether rates are fetched through DHL's XML or REST API.

field.summary: Weight unit sent to DHL.
field.usage: Whether package weights are sent to DHL in pounds or kilograms.

field.summary: Default package width sent to DHL.
field.usage: The package width used in DHL rate requests when specific dimensions are enabled.

field.summary: Your FedEx account number.
field.usage: The FedEx account used for rating and shipping.

field.summary: Offer live FedEx rates at checkout.
field.usage: When Yes, FedEx shipping rates are requested and offered to customers.

field.summary: Which FedEx services are offered.
field.usage: The FedEx services customers can choose from at checkout.

field.summary: Your FedEx API key.
field.usage: Credential for the FedEx rating API.

field.summary: Log FedEx API requests and responses.
field.usage: When Yes, FedEx API traffic is written to the debug log.

field.summary: Use the FedEx tracking API.
field.usage: When Yes, shipment tracking is retrieved via the FedEx tracking API, using its own credentials.

field.summary: FedEx service used for free shipping.
field.usage: The FedEx service applied when an order qualifies for free shipping.

field.summary: Offer free FedEx shipping above a subtotal.
field.usage: When enabled, FedEx shipping is free once the order meets the subtotal below.

field.summary: Order subtotal that qualifies for free FedEx shipping.
field.usage: Orders at or above this subtotal ship free via the chosen FedEx free method.

field.summary: Whether FedEx handling applies per order or per package.
field.usage: Whether the handling fee is charged once per order or for each package.

field.summary: A handling fee added to FedEx rates.
field.usage: An extra amount added on top of FedEx's returned rate.

field.summary: Whether the FedEx handling fee is fixed or a percentage.
field.usage: Whether the handling fee is a fixed amount or a percentage of the rate.

field.summary: Heaviest package FedEx will rate.
field.usage: Orders over this weight are split into multiple packages for rating.

field.summary: The default FedEx packaging type.
field.usage: The package type assumed when requesting FedEx rates.

field.summary: How packages are handed to FedEx.
field.usage: The drop-off or pickup arrangement used, which can affect rates.

field.summary: FedEx production API endpoint.
field.usage: The live FedEx web-services URL rates are requested from.

field.summary: Rate as residential delivery.
field.usage: When Yes, FedEx rates assume delivery to a residential address.

field.summary: Whether FedEx is limited to specific countries.
field.usage: Offer FedEx in all allowed countries, or restrict it to the countries chosen below.

field.summary: Use the FedEx test environment.
field.usage: When Yes, requests go to FedEx's sandbox instead of production.

field.summary: FedEx sandbox API endpoint.
field.usage: The test FedEx web-services URL used in sandbox mode.

field.summary: Your FedEx API secret key.
field.usage: Credential paired with the API key for the FedEx rating API.

field.summary: How multi-package orders are requested.
field.usage: Whether the order is divided into equal weights (one request) or rated from the origin weight.

field.summary: Show FedEx even when it returns no rates.
field.usage: When Yes, FedEx is shown (with its error message) instead of being hidden when it can't return rates.

field.summary: Your FedEx SmartPost hub ID.
field.usage: The SmartPost hub identifier required for SmartPost services.

field.summary: Position of FedEx among shipping methods.
field.usage: Controls where FedEx appears in the list of shipping options. Lower numbers appear first.

field.summary: The countries FedEx ships to.
field.usage: The countries where FedEx is offered, used when it is limited to specific countries.

field.summary: Message shown when FedEx is unavailable.
field.usage: The text shown to customers when FedEx can't return a rate.

field.summary: The carrier heading shown for FedEx.
field.usage: The group title shown above FedEx's rates at checkout.

field.summary: Your FedEx tracking API key.
field.usage: Credential for the FedEx tracking API.

field.summary: Your FedEx tracking API secret.
field.usage: Credential paired with the tracking API key.

field.summary: Weight unit sent to FedEx.
field.usage: Whether package weights are sent to FedEx in pounds or kilograms.

field.summary: Offer a single flat shipping rate.
field.usage: When Yes, Flat Rate shipping is available at checkout.

field.summary: A handling fee added to the Flat Rate price.
field.usage: An extra amount added on top of the flat shipping price.

field.summary: Whether the Flat Rate handling fee is fixed or a percentage.
field.usage: Whether the handling fee is a fixed amount or a percentage of the rate.

field.summary: The method name shown for Flat Rate.
field.usage: The shipping method label customers see, for example "Fixed".

field.summary: The flat shipping amount charged.
field.usage: The fixed shipping price, applied per order or per item depending on the type below.

field.summary: Whether Flat Rate is limited to specific countries.
field.usage: Offer Flat Rate in all allowed countries, or restrict it to the countries chosen below.

field.summary: Show Flat Rate even when it doesn't apply.
field.usage: When Yes, the method is shown (with its error message) instead of being hidden when unavailable.

field.summary: Position of Flat Rate among shipping methods.
field.usage: Controls where Flat Rate appears in the list of shipping options. Lower numbers appear first.

field.summary: The countries Flat Rate ships to.
field.usage: The countries where Flat Rate is offered, used when it is limited to specific countries.

field.summary: Message shown when Flat Rate is unavailable.
field.usage: The text shown to customers when Flat Rate can't be offered for their order.

field.summary: The carrier heading shown for Flat Rate.
field.usage: The group title shown above the Flat Rate method at checkout.

field.summary: Whether the flat rate is charged per order or per item.
field.usage: Whether the flat price is charged once per order or multiplied by the number of items.

field.summary: Offer free shipping above a subtotal.
field.usage: When Yes, Free Shipping is available once the order meets the minimum subtotal below.

field.summary: Minimum order subtotal that qualifies for free shipping.
field.usage: Orders at or above this subtotal are eligible for Free Shipping.

field.summary: The method name shown for Free Shipping.
field.usage: The shipping method label customers see.

field.summary: Whether Free Shipping is limited to specific countries.
field.usage: Offer Free Shipping in all allowed countries, or restrict it to the countries chosen below.

field.summary: Show Free Shipping even when it doesn't apply.
field.usage: When Yes, the method is shown (with its error message) instead of being hidden when unavailable.

field.summary: Position of Free Shipping among shipping methods.
field.usage: Controls where Free Shipping appears in the list of shipping options. Lower numbers appear first.

field.summary: The countries Free Shipping is offered in.
field.usage: The countries where Free Shipping is available, used when it is limited to specific countries.

field.summary: Message shown when Free Shipping is unavailable.
field.usage: The text shown to customers when Free Shipping can't be offered for their order.

field.summary: Compare the subtotal including tax.
field.usage: When Yes, tax is counted toward the free-shipping subtotal threshold.

field.summary: The carrier heading shown for Free Shipping.
field.usage: The group title shown above the Free Shipping method at checkout.

field.summary: Offer in-store pickup as a shipping method.
field.usage: When Yes, the In-Store Delivery method is available at checkout.

field.summary: The method name shown for In-Store Delivery.
field.usage: The shipping method label customers see.

field.summary: The amount charged for in-store delivery.
field.usage: The shipping price applied when the customer selects in-store pickup.

field.summary: How far to search for pickup locations.
field.usage: The radius within which nearby pickup/source locations are offered to the customer.

field.summary: Message shown when In-Store Delivery is unavailable.
field.usage: The text shown to customers when in-store pickup can't be offered.

field.summary: The carrier heading shown for In-Store Delivery.
field.usage: The group title shown above the In-Store Delivery method at checkout.

field.summary: Offer rates from an imported rate table.
field.usage: When Yes, Table Rates shipping is available, pricing orders from the imported rate table.

field.summary: What the rate table is keyed on.
field.usage: Whether table rates are looked up by weight, order price, or item count — each versus destination.

field.summary: Download the current rate table as CSV.
field.usage: Exports the configured table rates for this scope to a CSV file.

field.summary: A handling fee added to table rates.
field.usage: An extra amount added on top of the looked-up table rate.

field.summary: Whether the Table Rates handling fee is fixed or a percentage.
field.usage: Whether the handling fee is a fixed amount or a percentage of the rate.

field.summary: Upload a rate table from CSV.
field.usage: Imports table rates from a CSV file, replacing the current rates for this scope.

field.summary: Count virtual products in the rate calculation.
field.usage: When Yes, virtual products count toward the table-rate condition (price, weight, or quantity).

field.summary: The method name shown for Table Rates.
field.usage: The shipping method label customers see.

field.summary: Whether Table Rates is limited to specific countries.
field.usage: Offer Table Rates in all allowed countries, or restrict it to the countries chosen below.

field.summary: Show Table Rates even when no rate matches.
field.usage: When Yes, the method is shown (with its error message) instead of being hidden when no rate applies.

field.summary: Position of Table Rates among shipping methods.
field.usage: Controls where Table Rates appears in the list of shipping options. Lower numbers appear first.

field.summary: The countries Table Rates ships to.
field.usage: The countries where Table Rates is offered, used when it is limited to specific countries.

field.summary: Message shown when Table Rates is unavailable.
field.usage: The text shown to customers when no table rate matches their order.

field.summary: The carrier heading shown for Table Rates.
field.usage: The group title shown above the Table Rates method at checkout.

field.summary: Your UPS access license (API) number.
field.usage: Credential issued by UPS for API access.

field.summary: Offer live UPS rates at checkout.
field.usage: When Yes, UPS shipping rates are requested and offered to customers.

field.summary: Which UPS services are offered.
field.usage: The UPS services customers can choose from at checkout.

field.summary: The default UPS packaging type.
field.usage: The package type assumed when requesting UPS rates.

field.summary: Log UPS API requests and responses.
field.usage: When Yes, UPS API traffic is written to the debug log.

field.summary: Rate to a residential or commercial address.
field.usage: Whether UPS rates assume a residential or a commercial destination.

field.summary: UPS service used for free shipping.
field.usage: The UPS service applied when an order qualifies for free shipping.

field.summary: Offer free UPS shipping above a subtotal.
field.usage: When enabled, UPS shipping is free once the order meets the subtotal below.

field.summary: Order subtotal that qualifies for free UPS shipping.
field.usage: Orders at or above this subtotal ship free via the chosen UPS free method.

field.summary: UPS REST rating endpoint.
field.usage: The UPS REST API URL used to request rates.

field.summary: UPS rating endpoint (legacy XML).
field.usage: The UPS XML API URL used to request rates.

field.summary: UPS XML rate gateway URL.
field.usage: The endpoint for legacy XML rate requests.

field.summary: Whether UPS handling applies per order or per package.
field.usage: Whether the handling fee is charged once per order or for each package.

field.summary: A handling fee added to UPS rates.
field.usage: An extra amount added on top of UPS's returned rate.

field.summary: Whether the UPS handling fee is fixed or a percentage.
field.usage: Whether the handling fee is a fixed amount or a percentage of the rate.

field.summary: Include taxes in UPS rates.
field.usage: When Yes, any taxes UPS returns are included in the quoted rate.

field.summary: Use the live UPS account.
field.usage: When Yes, the production UPS account is used instead of a test account.

field.summary: Heaviest package UPS will rate.
field.usage: Orders over this weight are split into multiple packages for rating.

field.summary: Lightest package UPS will rate.
field.usage: The minimum weight sent to UPS for a package.

field.summary: Use the UPS development or live endpoint.
field.usage: Whether the legacy XML API talks to UPS's development or live servers.

field.summary: Use your negotiated UPS rates.
field.usage: When Yes, UPS returns your account's negotiated rates instead of published rates (requires a shipper number).

field.summary: The UPS origin/shipment region.
field.usage: The region your shipments originate from, which determines the available UPS services.

field.summary: Your UPS API password.
field.usage: Credential used to authenticate to the UPS API.

field.summary: How packages are given to UPS.
field.usage: The pickup arrangement used, which can affect the rates returned.

field.summary: Whether UPS is limited to specific countries.
field.usage: Offer UPS in all allowed countries, or restrict it to the countries chosen below.

field.summary: How multi-package orders are requested.
field.usage: Whether the order is divided into equal weights (one request) or rated from the origin weight.

field.summary: Your UPS shipper (account) number.
field.usage: The UPS account number, required for negotiated rates.

field.summary: Show UPS even when it returns no rates.
field.usage: When Yes, UPS is shown (with its error message) instead of being hidden when it can't return rates.

field.summary: Position of UPS among shipping methods.
field.usage: Controls where UPS appears in the list of shipping options. Lower numbers appear first.

field.summary: The countries UPS ships to.
field.usage: The countries where UPS is offered, used when it is limited to specific countries.

field.summary: Message shown when UPS is unavailable.
field.usage: The text shown to customers when UPS can't return a rate.

field.summary: The carrier heading shown for UPS.
field.usage: The group title shown above UPS's rates at checkout.

field.summary: UPS REST tracking endpoint.
field.usage: The UPS REST API URL used to track shipments.

field.summary: UPS tracking endpoint (legacy XML).
field.usage: The UPS XML API URL used to track shipments.

field.summary: Which UPS API to use.
field.usage: Selects the UPS integration — the modern REST API or the legacy XML API.

field.summary: Weight unit sent to UPS.
field.usage: Whether package weights are sent to UPS in pounds or kilograms.

field.summary: Your UPS API username.
field.usage: Credential used to authenticate to the UPS API.

field.summary: Your USPS payment account number.
field.usage: The USPS account used to pay for labels.

field.summary: The type of USPS payment account.
field.usage: Whether the account is an EPS or PERMIT account.

field.summary: Offer live USPS rates at checkout.
field.usage: When Yes, USPS shipping rates are requested and offered to customers.

field.summary: AES / ITN exemption code for customs.
field.usage: The AES Internal Transaction Number or exemption code sent on international shipments.

field.summary: Which USPS services are offered (legacy API).
field.usage: The USPS services customers can choose from when using the Web Tools API.

field.summary: Your USPS REST client ID.
field.usage: Credential for the USPS REST API.

field.summary: Your USPS REST client secret.
field.usage: Credential paired with the client ID for the USPS REST API.

field.summary: The default USPS container type.
field.usage: The package/container type assumed when requesting USPS rates.

field.summary: Your USPS Customer Registration ID (CRID).
field.usage: The USPS CRID tied to your business account.

field.summary: Log USPS API requests and responses.
field.usage: When Yes, USPS API traffic is written to the debug log.

field.summary: USPS service used for free shipping.
field.usage: The USPS service applied when an order qualifies for free shipping.

field.summary: Offer free USPS shipping above a subtotal.
field.usage: When enabled, USPS shipping is free once the order meets the subtotal below.

field.summary: Order subtotal that qualifies for free USPS shipping.
field.usage: Orders at or above this subtotal ship free via the chosen USPS free method.

field.summary: USPS REST development endpoint.
field.usage: The USPS REST API URL used in development mode.

field.summary: USPS REST production endpoint.
field.usage: The USPS REST API URL used in production.

field.summary: USPS secure endpoint (legacy Web Tools).
field.usage: The secure USPS Web Tools URL used for authenticated requests.

field.summary: USPS rating endpoint (legacy Web Tools).
field.usage: The USPS Web Tools URL used to request rates.

field.summary: Default package girth sent to USPS.
field.usage: The package girth used for USPS rates on non-rectangular parcels.

field.summary: Whether USPS handling applies per order or per package.
field.usage: Whether the handling fee is charged once per order or for each package.

field.summary: A handling fee added to USPS rates.
field.usage: An extra amount added on top of USPS's returned rate.

field.summary: Whether the USPS handling fee is fixed or a percentage.
field.usage: Whether the handling fee is a fixed amount or a percentage of the rate.

field.summary: Default package height sent to USPS.
field.usage: The package height used in USPS rate requests.

field.summary: Default package length sent to USPS.
field.usage: The package length used in USPS rate requests.

field.summary: Whether packages are machinable.
field.usage: Whether packages can be processed by USPS machines; non-machinable items may cost more.

field.summary: Heaviest package USPS will rate.
field.usage: Orders over this weight are split into multiple packages for rating.

field.summary: Your USPS Mailer ID (MID).
field.usage: The USPS Mailer ID used on shipments.

field.summary: Your USPS Manifest Mailer ID.
field.usage: The Mailer ID used for manifesting shipments.

field.summary: Use the USPS development or live endpoint.
field.usage: Whether requests go to USPS's development or production servers.

field.summary: Your USPS Web Tools password.
field.usage: Credential for the legacy USPS Web Tools API.

field.summary: Use commercial or retail USPS pricing.
field.usage: Whether rates use commercial (account) pricing or retail pricing.

field.summary: Which USPS services are offered (REST API).
field.usage: The USPS services customers can choose from when using the REST API.

field.summary: Whether USPS is limited to specific countries.
field.usage: Offer USPS in all allowed countries, or restrict it to the countries chosen below.

field.summary: How multi-package orders are requested.
field.usage: Whether the order is divided into equal weights (one request) or rated from the origin weight.

field.summary: Show USPS even when it returns no rates.
field.usage: When Yes, USPS is shown (with its error message) instead of being hidden when it can't return rates.

field.summary: The USPS package size class.
field.usage: Whether the package is Regular or Large by USPS size rules.

field.summary: Position of USPS among shipping methods.
field.usage: Controls where USPS appears in the list of shipping options. Lower numbers appear first.

field.summary: The countries USPS ships to.
field.usage: The countries where USPS is offered, used when it is limited to specific countries.

field.summary: Message shown when USPS is unavailable.
field.usage: The text shown to customers when USPS can't return a rate.

field.summary: The carrier heading shown for USPS.
field.usage: The group title shown above USPS's rates at checkout.

field.summary: Your USPS Web Tools user ID.
field.usage: Credential for the legacy USPS Web Tools API.

field.summary: Which USPS API to use.
field.usage: Selects the USPS integration — the modern REST APIs or the legacy Web Tools API.

field.summary: Default package width sent to USPS.
field.usage: The package width used in USPS rate requests.

field.summary: The order of day, month and year in custom date option inputs.
field.usage: Sets how date-type custom options are laid out on the storefront — for example day/month/year versus month/day/year.

field.summary: Whether custom time options use 12- or 24-hour format.
field.usage: Controls the clock format shown for date/time custom options on product pages.

field.summary: Show a calendar picker for date custom options.
field.usage: When Yes, date custom options use a calendar widget instead of plain dropdowns.

field.summary: The range of years offered in date custom options.
field.usage: Limits the selectable years for date custom options, entered as a four-digit from,to range. Leave blank for the default range.

field.summary: Whether downloadable files download or open in the browser.
field.usage: Sets the Content-Disposition for downloadable links — force a download, or open the file inline in the browser.

field.summary: Require an account when the cart has downloadable items.
field.usage: When Yes, orders containing downloadable products require a customer account (guest checkout is blocked), unless the product's links are shareable.

field.summary: Default number of downloads allowed per purchased link.
field.usage: The default download limit applied to new downloadable links. Leave blank or 0 for unlimited.

field.summary: Open downloadable links in a new browser window.
field.usage: When Yes, download links open in a new tab or window.

field.summary: Default heading shown above a product's downloadable links.
field.usage: The default title for the Links section on downloadable product pages (for example, "Links").

field.summary: When a purchased download becomes available.
field.usage: Whether access to downloads is granted once the order is Pending, or only after it is Invoiced (paid).

field.summary: Default heading shown above a product's sample files.
field.usage: The default title for the Samples section on downloadable product pages (for example, "Samples").

field.summary: Allow downloadable links to be used without signing in.
field.usage: When Yes, downloadable links are shareable and can be accessed without a customer account, which also permits guest checkout for them.

field.summary: Template for auto-generating a product's meta description.
field.usage: Pattern used to build the meta description when a product has none. Supports placeholders such as {{name}} and {{description}}.

field.summary: Template for auto-generating a product's meta keywords.
field.usage: Pattern used to build meta keywords when a product has none. Supports placeholders such as {{name}} and {{sku}}.

field.summary: Template for auto-generating a product's meta title.
field.usage: Pattern used to build the meta title when a product has none. Supports the {{name}} placeholder.

field.summary: Template for auto-generating a product SKU.
field.usage: Pattern used to build a SKU when none is entered. Supports the {{name}} placeholder.

field.summary: The default product sort order on category pages.
field.usage: Which sort shoppers see first on category listings, unless an individual category overrides it.

field.summary: Direction of the default category sort.
field.usage: Whether the default category sort runs ascending or descending.

field.summary: Use the flat category index on the storefront.
field.usage: When Yes, the storefront reads categories from the flat index — a legacy performance option. Flat catalog is deprecated and is usually left No.

field.summary: Use the flat product index on the storefront.
field.usage: When Yes, the storefront reads products from the flat index — a legacy performance option. Flat catalog is deprecated and is usually left No.

field.summary: Default number of products per page in grid mode.
field.usage: The pre-selected "per page" count for grid view. Must be one of the allowed values below.

field.summary: The selectable per-page counts for grid mode.
field.usage: Comma-separated list of "products per page" choices offered to shoppers in grid view.

field.summary: Offer an "All" option in the per-page dropdown.
field.usage: When Yes, shoppers can choose to show every product on one page. Use with care on large categories.

field.summary: Which view modes (grid/list) category pages offer.
field.usage: Sets whether category pages show a grid, a list, or both with one as the default.

field.summary: Default number of products per page in list mode.
field.usage: The pre-selected "per page" count for list view. Must be one of the allowed values below.

field.summary: The selectable per-page counts for list mode.
field.usage: Comma-separated list of "products per page" choices offered to shoppers in list view.

field.summary: Remember each shopper's page-size and sort choices.
field.usage: When Yes, pagination and sort selections persist for the shopper across pages. May affect SEO and increase the number of cached page variations.

field.summary: Show a preview tooltip when hovering a swatch.
field.usage: When Yes, hovering a colour or image swatch shows an enlarged preview tooltip.

field.summary: Show configurable swatches on category listings.
field.usage: When Yes, swatches appear on product tiles in category and search results, not only on the product page.

field.summary: Maximum swatches shown per product in listings.
field.usage: Caps how many swatches are displayed on a product tile in listings before the rest are truncated.

field.summary: Show the category filter in layered navigation.
field.usage: When Yes, a category filter appears in layered navigation on listing pages.

field.summary: Show the product count next to each filter option.
field.usage: When Yes, each layered-navigation option shows how many products match it.

field.summary: Minimum products before a price range is subdivided.
field.usage: Price intervals holding fewer products than this are not split further in layered navigation.

field.summary: Collapse identical prices into a single interval.
field.usage: When Yes, products that all share one price are grouped into a single price filter rather than a range.

field.summary: How price-filter ranges are calculated.
field.usage: Whether layered-navigation price ranges are built automatically (by equal spans or equal product counts) or from a fixed manual step.

field.summary: Maximum number of price intervals shown.
field.usage: Caps how many price ranges layered navigation displays (up to 100).

field.summary: The fixed price step used for manual ranges.
field.usage: The width of each price interval when the range calculation is set to Manual.

field.summary: How many category levels appear in the top menu.
field.usage: The maximum category depth rendered in the storefront top navigation. 0 means no limit.

field.summary: Fallback image shown when a product has no image.
field.usage: The default placeholder used wherever a product is missing its own image, set per image role (base, small, thumbnail, swatch).

field.summary: Whether product prices are global or set per website.
field.usage: Sets the scope of catalog prices. Global uses one price everywhere; Website allows a different price per website. Changing it can affect existing prices and must line up with your base-currency scope.

field.summary: Autoplay the base video on the product page.
field.usage: When Yes, the product's base video plays automatically when the page opens.

field.summary: Show related YouTube videos after playback.
field.usage: When Yes, YouTube may display related videos when a product video finishes.

field.summary: Loop product videos when they finish.
field.usage: When Yes, a product video restarts automatically after it ends.

field.summary: YouTube Data API key used to embed product videos.
field.usage: The API key required to load and play YouTube videos on product pages.

field.summary: Let customers subscribe to price-drop alerts.
field.usage: When Yes, a "notify me when the price drops" option appears on product pages.

field.summary: Let customers subscribe to back-in-stock alerts.
field.usage: When Yes, a "notify me when back in stock" option appears on out-of-stock products.

field.summary: Address that receives product-alert cron error reports.
field.usage: The email notified if the product-alert cron job fails.

field.summary: The sender identity for cron error emails.
field.usage: Which store email identity sends product-alert cron error notifications.

field.summary: The template for product-alert cron error emails.
field.usage: The transactional template used to report product-alert cron failures.

field.summary: How often product-alert emails are sent.
field.usage: The schedule on which the product-alert cron job runs and sends queued price and stock alerts.

field.summary: Time of day the product-alert cron runs.
field.usage: The clock time at which the product-alert job runs on its scheduled days.

field.summary: The store identity price/stock alert emails are sent from.
field.usage: Which store email identity (sender) is used for product-alert emails.

field.summary: The email template used for price-drop alerts.
field.usage: The transactional template used when sending price-alert emails.

field.summary: The email template used for back-in-stock alerts.
field.usage: The transactional template used when sending stock-alert emails.

field.summary: How many compared products to keep per shopper.
field.usage: The maximum number of items retained in a shopper's "recently compared" list.

field.summary: How long recently-compared entries are kept (seconds).
field.usage: Lifetime, in seconds, of a shopper's recently-compared product records.

field.summary: How long recently-viewed entries are kept (seconds).
field.usage: Lifetime, in seconds, of a shopper's recently-viewed product records.

field.summary: The scope recently viewed/compared lists are shared across.
field.usage: Whether a shopper's recently viewed and compared products are shared per website, per store, or per store view.

field.summary: Persist recently viewed/compared lists server-side.
field.usage: When Yes, these lists are saved on the server so they follow a signed-in customer across devices.

field.summary: How many viewed products to keep per shopper.
field.usage: The maximum number of items retained in a shopper's "recently viewed" list.

field.summary: Enable product reviews on the storefront.
field.usage: When Yes, customers can read and submit product reviews.

field.summary: Let guests submit product reviews.
field.usage: When Yes, shoppers can post reviews without an account. When No, only signed-in customers can.

field.summary: Maximum suggestions shown in search autocomplete.
field.usage: Caps how many suggestions appear in the search-box dropdown as a shopper types.

field.summary: Require authentication to connect to Elasticsearch 8.
field.usage: When Yes, Magento sends the username and password below when connecting to Elasticsearch.

field.summary: Prefix for the Elasticsearch indexes Magento creates.
field.usage: Namespaces this installation's indexes so several stores can share one Elasticsearch cluster without clashing.

field.summary: The minimum-should-match rule for Elasticsearch queries.
field.usage: Controls how many query terms must match. Uses Elasticsearch's minimum_should_match syntax.

field.summary: Password for the Elasticsearch connection.
field.usage: The password Magento uses when Elasticsearch authentication is enabled.

field.summary: Hostname of the Elasticsearch server.
field.usage: The host Magento connects to for Elasticsearch.

field.summary: Port of the Elasticsearch server.
field.usage: The TCP port Magento uses to reach Elasticsearch.

field.summary: Connection timeout for Elasticsearch, in seconds.
field.usage: How long Magento waits for Elasticsearch to respond before giving up.

field.summary: Test the connection to Elasticsearch.
field.usage: Runs a live check that Magento can reach Elasticsearch with the settings above.

field.summary: Username for the Elasticsearch connection.
field.usage: The username Magento uses when Elasticsearch authentication is enabled.

field.summary: Use the product EAV indexer to speed up indexing.
field.usage: When Yes, the product EAV indexer is enabled to speed up indexation. Make sure your search engine is configured to support it.

field.summary: The search engine powering catalog search.
field.usage: Selects the backend used for product search and indexing. If left unset, the default engine is used.

field.summary: How many popular search terms are cached.
field.usage: The number of popular search terms kept in cache for faster responses.

field.summary: Maximum length of a search query.
field.usage: Queries longer than this are truncated. Must be compatible with the matching setting in your search engine.

field.summary: Minimum length of a search query.
field.usage: Queries shorter than this are ignored. Must be compatible with the matching setting in your search engine.

field.summary: Require authentication to connect to OpenSearch.
field.usage: When Yes, Magento sends the username and password below when connecting to OpenSearch.

field.summary: Prefix for the OpenSearch indexes Magento creates.
field.usage: Namespaces this installation's indexes so several stores can share one OpenSearch cluster without clashing.

field.summary: The minimum-should-match rule for OpenSearch queries.
field.usage: Controls how many query terms must match. Uses OpenSearch's minimum_should_match syntax.

field.summary: Password for the OpenSearch connection.
field.usage: The password Magento uses when OpenSearch authentication is enabled.

field.summary: Hostname of the OpenSearch server.
field.usage: The host Magento connects to for OpenSearch.

field.summary: Port of the OpenSearch server.
field.usage: The TCP port Magento uses to reach OpenSearch.

field.summary: Connection timeout for OpenSearch, in seconds.
field.usage: How long Magento waits for OpenSearch to respond before giving up.

field.summary: Test the connection to OpenSearch.
field.usage: Runs a live check that Magento can reach OpenSearch with the settings above.

field.summary: Username for the OpenSearch connection.
field.usage: The username Magento uses when OpenSearch authentication is enabled.

field.summary: How many search recommendations to show.
field.usage: The number of recommended terms displayed for a search.

field.summary: Show result counts next to search recommendations.
field.usage: When Yes, each recommendation shows how many results it would return.

field.summary: Offer alternative-term recommendations for searches.
field.usage: When Yes, searches suggest related terms. May slow the site on large catalogs.

field.summary: How many search suggestions to show.
field.usage: The number of "did you mean" suggestions offered for a search.

field.summary: Show result counts next to search suggestions.
field.usage: When Yes, each suggestion shows how many results it would return.

field.summary: Offer spelling suggestions for searches.
field.usage: When Yes, misspelled searches receive "did you mean" suggestions. May slow the site on large catalogs.

field.summary: Add a canonical link tag to category pages.
field.usage: When Yes, category pages emit a canonical URL to reduce duplicate-content issues in search engines.

field.summary: Suffix appended to category URLs (e.g. .html).
field.usage: The suffix added to category URL keys. Refresh the cache after changing it.

field.summary: Generate URL rewrites for products under categories.
field.usage: When Yes, products get category-path URLs. Warning: turning this off permanently removes existing category/product URL rewrites.

field.summary: Add a canonical link tag to product pages.
field.usage: When Yes, product pages emit a canonical URL to reduce duplicate-content issues in search engines.

field.summary: Scope used when generating product URL rewrites.
field.usage: Whether product URL rewrites are generated at the website or the store-view level when a product is edited.

field.summary: Suffix appended to product URLs (e.g. .html).
field.usage: The suffix added to product URL keys. Refresh the cache after changing it.

field.summary: Transliterate accented characters in product URLs.
field.usage: When Yes, non-ASCII characters in URL keys are converted to ASCII equivalents.

field.summary: Include the category path in product URLs.
field.usage: When Yes, product URLs include their category path (for example /category/product).

field.summary: Keep a redirect when a URL key changes.
field.usage: When Yes, changing a product or category URL key creates a permanent (301) redirect from the old URL.

field.summary: Make the storefront search-terms page available.
field.usage: When Enabled, the popular-search-terms page is accessible to shoppers and search-engine crawlers.

field.summary: Character separating the parts of page titles.
field.usage: The separator placed between segments of SEO page titles — for example a dash or a pipe.

field.summary: Yes runs bulk inventory actions via the message queue; requires a running queue consumer.
field.usage: Yes routes admin bulk inventory actions through the message queue so large updates run in the background instead of blocking the admin screen. It needs a running queue consumer; without one the queued jobs never process.

field.summary: How many items are processed per batch in asynchronous admin bulk operations.
field.usage: Sets the number of records handled in each batch when admin bulk stock/source operations run asynchronously. Applies only when asynchronous bulk operations are enabled. Larger batches finish in fewer passes but use more memory per run.

field.summary: Sync vs async reindex of stock/source data; async offloads the work to the message queue.
field.usage: Chooses whether stock/source index updates run inline or are queued for asynchronous processing. As the field note says, async mode needs a configured queue manager (consumers running). Async keeps admin saves and imports fast by deferring the reindex off the request.

field.summary: Whether refunding an item automatically returns its quantity to stock.
field.usage: When Yes, the Return to Stock option is ticked by default when a credit memo is created, so refunded quantities go back into inventory. Staff can still change it per credit memo.

field.summary: Whether customers can order more than the quantity in stock.
field.usage:
Controls what happens when a shopper orders beyond available stock. Allowing backorders lets quantity fall below zero so the order is still accepted.

Changing this reprocesses the whole catalog, so it can take some time.

field.summary: Whether products must be purchased in fixed multiples.
field.usage: Turns on quantity increments, forcing shoppers to buy in multiples of the Qty Increments value below — for example, in packs of 6.

field.summary: Master switch for whether Magento tracks inventory quantities at all.
field.usage:
When Yes, Magento tracks quantities and enforces stock status for products that use the default settings. When No, products are always treated as available and quantity is ignored.

Changing this reprocesses the whole catalog, so it can take some time.

field.summary: The largest quantity of a single product a customer may buy in one order.
field.usage: Caps how many of one product can be placed in the cart. Applies to products using the default inventory settings; a per-product value overrides it.

field.summary: The quantity at which a product is considered out of stock.
field.usage: When available stock drops to this number, the product is marked Out of Stock. A negative value — together with backorders — lets stock fall below zero while the product stays sellable.

field.summary: The smallest quantity of a product a customer must buy in one order.
field.usage: Sets the minimum quantity required to add a product to the cart. Can be set per customer group, and overridden per product.

field.summary: The stock level at or below which a product is flagged as low on admin reports.
field.usage: Sets the quantity that marks a product as low on stock for the admin Low Stock report and notifications. It does not affect whether the product can be sold.

field.summary: The multiple in which a product must be purchased when increments are enabled.
field.usage: The step size shoppers must order in — for example 6 means quantities of 6, 12, 18 and so on. Only applies when Enable Qty Increments is set to Yes.

field.summary: Whether cancelling an order can flip a product back to "In Stock".
field.usage: When an order is cancelled and its items return to stock, this decides whether a product that had dropped to Out of Stock is automatically set back to In Stock. Applies only while stock is being managed.

field.summary: Whether placing an order immediately reduces a product's stock quantity.
field.usage: Controls whether Magento subtracts ordered quantities from stock the moment an order is placed. In most setups this should stay Yes so available quantity reflects open orders; set it to No only when an external system owns stock levels.

field.summary: Whether the storefront shows a product's "In Stock" / "Out of Stock" availability.
field.usage: Controls whether the stock-availability label is shown to shoppers on product pages. Setting it to No hides the availability line without changing how stock is tracked.

field.summary: Yes re-checks stock on every cart load (accurate, more queries); No is faster but skips that validation.
field.usage: When Yes, cart item stock is re-validated each time the cart loads, keeping availability accurate at the cost of extra queries. When No, that pre-validation is skipped for a faster cart, but out-of-stock items may linger until checkout.

field.summary: Which message shoppers see when they request more than the available quantity.
field.usage: Chooses the wording shown when a customer tries to add more of a product than is in stock.

field.summary: Whether out-of-stock products appear in category listings and search results.
field.usage:
When Yes, products with no available stock still appear in category pages, search and layered navigation. When No, they are hidden from listings but remain reachable by their direct product URL.

Changing this invalidates the catalog and search indexes, so the storefront keeps the previous behaviour until reindexing completes.

field.summary: Quantity at or below which the storefront shows an "Only X left" message.
field.usage: Sets the low-stock quantity that triggers the Only X left urgency message on the product page. Set it to 0 to turn the message off entirely.

field.summary: Whether inventory data is auto-synced when the catalog changes.
field.usage: When Yes, inventory stock and source data is kept in step automatically as products are added to or removed from the catalog. When No, that reconciliation must be triggered manually. Global scope.

field.summary: Adds a Delete mass action to the Reservations grid, able to remove even uncompensated reservations.
field.usage: Beyond the native note: this exposes a Delete mass action on the inventory Reservations grid (gated by ACL) that drops reservations outright, unlike Clean which only clears compensated ones. It is a global setting — leave it off except for deliberate recovery, since deleting live reservations can desync salable quantity.

field.summary: Google key used to geocode and measure distances for distance-based source selection; stored encrypted. Needs Geocoding + Distance Matrix APIs.
field.usage: The Google API key distance-based source selection uses to geocode addresses and compute shipping distances to sources. Per the native note, both the Geocoding and Distance Matrix APIs must be enabled on the key, or source selection cannot rank sources. Stored encrypted.

field.summary: The travel mode Google uses to measure distance — driving, walking, or bicycling.
field.usage: Chooses the Google travel mode for distance calculation: Driving, Walking, or Bicycling. Used when the Google distance provider is selected.

field.summary: Whether sources are ranked by physical distance or by travel time.
field.usage: Chooses the metric Google returns for ranking sources: Distance (physical distance) or Time to destination (travel time). Used when the Google distance provider is selected.

field.summary: Which distance provider is used to rank sources for distance-based source selection.
field.usage: Selects the service that calculates the distance between a shipping destination and each source when the Distance Based source selection algorithm runs.

field.summary: How a guest cart merges with the saved cart at login.
field.usage: When a guest signs in and both carts hold the same product, this decides whose quantity wins — or whether the two are added together.

field.summary: Which image represents a configurable product in the cart.
field.usage: Whether the cart shows the chosen variation's own thumbnail or the parent configurable product's thumbnail.

field.summary: Show cross-sell products on the cart page.
field.usage: When Yes, the shopping cart displays cross-sell product suggestions.

field.summary: How long an abandoned cart (quote) is kept (days).
field.usage: The number of days an inactive quote is retained before the cron job clears it.

field.summary: Show a "Clear Shopping Cart" button.
field.usage: When Yes, shoppers get a button to empty the whole cart at once.

field.summary: Which image represents a grouped product in the cart.
field.usage: Whether the cart shows each associated item's own thumbnail or the parent grouped product's thumbnail.

field.summary: What the header cart link counts.
field.usage: Whether the cart link in the header shows the number of distinct items or the total quantity of units.

field.summary: Cart items shown before pagination kicks in.
field.usage: The number of line items displayed on the cart page before a pager appears.

field.summary: Send shoppers to the cart after adding a product.
field.usage: When Yes, adding a product redirects to the cart page. When No, the shopper stays on the current page.

field.summary: Where the billing address is collected during checkout.
field.usage: Whether the billing address appears on the payment step or on its own dedicated checkout page.

field.summary: Require shoppers to accept terms and conditions.
field.usage: When Yes, the configured checkout agreements (terms & conditions) must be accepted before an order can be placed.

field.summary: Let guests check whether an email already has an account.
field.usage: When Yes, unauthenticated shoppers can query whether an email is already registered. Turning it off helps prevent account enumeration.

field.summary: Allow ordering without creating an account.
field.usage: When Yes, customers can check out as a guest. When No, they must register or sign in to place an order.

field.summary: Maximum order items shown on the checkout review.
field.usage: Caps how many line items are listed in the order summary during checkout.

field.summary: Enable the standard one-page checkout.
field.usage: When Yes, the built-in one-page checkout is available. Turning it off is usually done only when a custom checkout replaces it.

field.summary: How copies of payment-failed emails are sent.
field.usage: Whether additional recipients are blind-copied on one email or each sent a separate copy.

field.summary: Extra recipients of payment-failed notifications.
field.usage: Comma-separated email addresses that also receive payment-failure notices.

field.summary: The store identity payment-failed emails are sent from.
field.usage: Which store email identity (sender) is used for payment-failure emails.

field.summary: The store contact that receives payment-failed emails.
field.usage: Which store identity is notified when a customer's payment fails.

field.summary: The email template for payment-failed notifications.
field.usage: The transactional template used when a payment attempt fails at checkout.

field.summary: How many items the mini-cart lists.
field.usage: The number of recent items shown in the mini-cart dropdown.

field.summary: Show the mini-cart in the header.
field.usage: When Yes, the mini-cart dropdown is available from the header cart icon.

field.summary: Maximum items shown in the mini-cart before scrolling.
field.usage: Caps how many items the mini-cart displays before the list scrolls.

field.summary: Number of columns in new Page Builder column layouts; changing it affects newly added content only, not existing pages.
field.usage: The default number of columns a new Page Builder column container offers. Raising or lowering it changes the grid for content created afterward; existing pages keep the grid they were built with.

field.summary: Upper limit on the number of columns a Page Builder column layout can hold.
field.usage: Sets the maximum grid size, which caps how many columns editors can add to a Page Builder row. Raising it allows denser layouts; lowering it constrains content authors. Default scope.

field.summary: Previews Page Builder content on product and category edit pages; No can improve admin performance.
field.usage: Renders a live Page Builder preview on product and category edit pages. Applies only when Page Builder is enabled. As the native note says, setting No can speed up the admin when several attributes are Page Builder-editable, at the cost of the inline preview.

field.summary: Turning Page Builder off reverts content editing to the legacy editor, where existing PB content may not render.
field.usage: When Yes, Page Builder's layout tools are available for CMS content and as a product-attribute input type. Turning it off reverts editing to the legacy WYSIWYG, where content already built in Page Builder may not display correctly.

field.summary: Google Maps API key enabling Page Builder's Map content type; maps won't render without it.
field.usage: The Google Maps API key that authorizes Page Builder's Map content type to render maps; without a valid key, maps do not display. Usage is billed by Google, so restrict the key to your own domains.

field.summary: Custom Google Maps style JSON that restyles the Page Builder Map content type.
field.usage: Holds the Google Maps style JSON that, as the field note says, changes the look and feel of the Map content type in Page Builder. Leave it empty for the default map appearance; paste a valid style array to recolor or simplify the map.

field.summary: Dropbox app credentials (key/secret/refresh token) that let Page Builder sync templates to and from Dropbox; stored serialized.
field.usage: Holds the Dropbox App key, secret and refresh token Page Builder uses to import/export templates from a Dropbox repository. The native note explains how to generate the refresh token; without valid credentials the sync won't connect. Applies only when the feature is enabled (depends). Global setting (default scope).

field.summary: Turns Page Builder template import and export on or off.
field.usage: When set to Yes, the import and export actions for Page Builder templates are available in the admin, letting you move templates between stores.

field.summary: Yes syncs remote Page Builder templates from Dropbox on a schedule instead of on demand; suited to large libraries.
field.usage: When Yes, remote Page Builder templates are pulled from Dropbox by cron rather than fetched manually — recommended for large remote libraries. It requires the pbTemplateImport consumer in env.php, and re-saving this config before creating new credentials (per the note). Default scope.

field.summary: Selects which WYSIWYG editor adapter is used for content fields.
field.usage: Selects the WYSIWYG editor adapter used for rich-text content fields. Relates to the Enable WYSIWYG Editor setting. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Whether and how the WYSIWYG rich-text editor is available for content fields.
field.usage: Controls whether the WYSIWYG rich-text editor is available for content fields and how it is presented. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: Yes hardcodes media URLs (break if base URL changes); No keeps dynamic references.
field.usage: Yes inserts media as absolute static URLs; because they are hardcoded they break if you later change the base URL. No stores dynamic references that follow the base URL. Applies only when the WYSIWYG editor is disabled.

field.summary: Turns the storefront Contact Us page and form on or off.
field.usage: Controls whether the Contact Us page and its /contact form are available on the storefront. Set to No to remove the page entirely. Can be set per website or store view, so the form can be live on one store and hidden on another.

field.summary: Template for Contact Us form emails; Default follows theme fallback, custom overrides it.
field.usage: The email template used for messages sent from the Contact Us form. Default follows theme fallback; pick a custom template to override it. Applies only when Contact Us is enabled, and can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The email address that receives messages submitted through the Contact Us form.
field.usage: The inbox that Contact Us submissions are delivered to. Applies only when Enable Contact Us is set to Yes. Can differ per website or store view, so each store can route enquiries to its own team.

field.summary: Which store email identity the Contact Us notification is sent from.
field.usage: Selects the sender identity used for the Contact Us notification — one of the Store Email Addresses identities (General Contact, Sales Representative, Customer Support, Custom 1/2), configured under Stores → Configuration → General → Store Email Addresses. Applies only when Enable Contact Us is Yes.

field.summary: Where CSP violation reports from admin pages are sent; the fallback for pages without their own URI.
field.usage: Endpoint that receives CSP violation reports for admin pages (the fallback for any admin page without its own URI). Collecting reports lets you tune the policy and spot blocked resources before switching admin CSP from report-only to enforced. Can differ per scope.

field.summary: URL that CSP violation reports for admin order creation are sent to; blank uses the default.
field.usage: Where the browser posts Content-Security-Policy violation reports for the admin Create Order page. Leave empty to use the admin area's default report URI per the native note. Website/store scoped.

field.summary: Where CSP violation reports from one-page checkout are sent; falls back to the storefront default.
field.usage: Endpoint that receives Content-Security-Policy violation reports for the one-page checkout. If empty, the storefront default report URI is used. Lets you monitor blocked scripts on checkout without enforcing the policy. Can differ per website/store view.

field.summary: Where browsers send CSP violation reports; use it in report-only mode before enforcing a stricter policy.
field.usage: URI that browsers POST CSP violation reports to, for storefront pages without their own report URI. Point it at a collector and run report-only mode first to see what a stricter policy would block before you enforce it. Can differ per website/store.

field.summary: The API key used to authenticate with the Currency Converter API service.
field.usage: The credential for the Currency Converter API rate provider. Stored encrypted.

field.summary: How many seconds to wait for the Currency Converter API service before timing out.
field.usage: The connection timeout, in seconds, for currency rate requests to the Currency Converter API service.

field.summary: API key for the legacy Fixer.io currency feed; stored encrypted.
field.usage: The key for fetching exchange rates from Fixer.io. As the field note says, use this only for keys generated at Fixer.io directly; keys from ApiLayer belong in the separate Fixer-via-APILayer field. It is stored encrypted at rest.

field.summary: The API key used to authenticate with the Fixer (APILayer) exchange-rate service.
field.usage: The credential for the Fixer API (APILayer) currency rate provider. Stored encrypted.

field.summary: How many seconds to wait for the Fixer (APILayer) rate service before timing out.
