field.usage: The connection timeout, in seconds, for currency rate requests to the Fixer API (APILayer) service.

field.summary: How many seconds to wait for the legacy Fixer.io rate service before timing out.
field.usage: The connection timeout, in seconds, for currency rate requests to the legacy Fixer.io service.

field.summary: Whether exchange rates are imported automatically on a schedule.
field.usage: When Yes, currency rates are fetched automatically from the configured service on the chosen frequency. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The email address notified when a scheduled currency rate import fails.
field.usage: The recipient for failure notifications from the scheduled rate import. Applies only when scheduled import is Enabled. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Which store email identity sends the scheduled-import failure notification.
field.usage: Selects the sender identity for rate-import failure emails — one of the Store Email Addresses identities (General Contact, Sales Representative, Customer Support, Custom 1/2). Applies only when scheduled import is Enabled. Can differ per website.

field.summary: Template for the alert sent when a scheduled currency-rate import fails; applies only when scheduled import is enabled. Per website.
field.usage: The email template used to notify staff when the scheduled currency-rate import errors out. Applies only when scheduled import is enabled; 'Default' resolves through theme fallback. Scoped per website.

field.summary: How often the scheduled currency rate import runs.
field.usage: The cron frequency for the automatic rate import: Daily, Weekly, or Monthly. Applies only when scheduled import is Enabled. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Which exchange-rate provider the scheduled import pulls rates from.
field.usage: Selects the rate service used by the scheduled import (the configured currency import providers). Applies only when scheduled import is Enabled. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The time of day the scheduled currency rate import runs.
field.usage: The start time (hour, minute, second) for the automatic rate import. Applies only when scheduled import is Enabled. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The currencies shoppers can switch between on the storefront.
field.usage: The set of currencies made available on the storefront; the Default Display Currency must be one of them. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Currency prices are stored and payments charged in; changing it needs prices and rates rechecked.
field.usage: The currency all product prices are stored in and every online payment is charged in; its scope follows Catalog Price Scope. Changing it does not reconvert stored prices, so review currency rates and prices afterwards. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The currency the storefront displays prices in by default.
field.usage: The base display currency shown to shoppers. It must be one of the Allowed Currencies. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Email template sent when a customer changes both email and password.
field.usage: The transactional template used to confirm a combined email-and-password change on the account.

field.summary: Email template sent when a customer changes their email address.
field.usage: The transactional template used to confirm an email-address change on the account.

field.summary: Require email confirmation before a new account can sign in.
field.usage: When Yes, new customers must click a confirmation link in an email before they can log in.

field.summary: Expose the customer's group through the GraphQL API.
field.usage: When No, customer group details are withheld from GraphQL responses — useful when group names are commercially sensitive.

field.summary: Whether customer accounts are shared across all websites or per website.
field.usage: Global lets a customer sign in on any website with one account; Per Website scopes each account to the website where it was created.

field.summary: Whether the Company field is shown and required.
field.usage: Controls the Company field on customer and address forms — optional, required, or hidden.

field.summary: Whether the Date of Birth field is shown and required.
field.usage: Controls the Date of Birth field on customer forms — optional, required, or hidden.

field.summary: Whether the Fax field is shown and required.
field.usage: Controls the Fax field on address forms — optional, required, or hidden.

field.summary: Whether the Gender field is shown and required.
field.usage: Controls the Gender field on customer forms — optional, required, or hidden.

field.summary: Show the Middle Name/Initial field.
field.usage: When Yes, a Middle Name/Initial field appears on name forms. It is always optional.

field.summary: The selectable name prefixes (Mr., Mrs., …).
field.usage: Semicolon-separated list of name prefixes offered as a dropdown. Leave empty to show a free-text field instead.

field.summary: Whether the name Prefix field is shown and required.
field.usage: Controls the Prefix field — the title before a name, such as Mr. or Mrs. — optional, required, or hidden.

field.summary: How many street address lines to show (1–4).
field.usage: The number of street-address input lines on address forms. Valid range is 1 to 4.

field.summary: The selectable name suffixes (Jr., Sr., …).
field.usage: Semicolon-separated list of name suffixes offered as a dropdown. Leave empty to show a free-text field instead.

field.summary: Whether the name Suffix field is shown and required.
field.usage: Controls the Suffix field — the part after a name, such as Jr. or Sr. — optional, required, or hidden.

field.summary: Whether the Tax/VAT Number field is shown and required.
field.usage: Controls the Tax/VAT number field on customer and address forms — optional, required, or hidden.

field.summary: Whether the Phone Number field is shown and required.
field.usage: Controls the Phone Number field on address forms — optional, required, or hidden.

field.summary: The HTML layout used to render a customer address.
field.usage: Template that formats addresses in HTML contexts such as account pages and emails. Supports a limited set of tags (b, br, p, strong, …).

field.summary: The single-line format used to render an address.
field.usage: Template that renders an address on one line, used in grids and summaries.

field.summary: The layout used to render addresses in PDF documents.
field.usage: Template that formats addresses on PDF invoices, shipments and credit memos.

field.summary: The plain-text format used to render an address.
field.usage: Template that renders an address as plain text, used in plain-text emails.

field.summary: Make CAPTCHA answers case-sensitive.
field.usage: When Yes, the customer must match the letter case of the CAPTCHA exactly.

field.summary: Turn on CAPTCHA for storefront customer forms.
field.usage: When Yes, a CAPTCHA is shown on the storefront forms selected below.

field.summary: Failed logins before CAPTCHA appears on the login form.
field.usage: The number of failed attempts after which CAPTCHA is required on login. 0 makes it always show.

field.summary: The font used to render the CAPTCHA image.
field.usage: The typeface used when drawing CAPTCHA characters.

field.summary: Which storefront forms show a CAPTCHA.
field.usage: The customer-facing forms protected by CAPTCHA — login, create account, forgot password, and so on.

field.summary: How many characters the CAPTCHA contains.
field.usage: The CAPTCHA length, up to 8 characters. A range such as 3-5 picks a random length each time.

field.summary: When the CAPTCHA is shown.
field.usage: Whether the CAPTCHA appears on every attempt, or only after a number of failed attempts.

field.summary: The character set CAPTCHAs are drawn from.
field.usage: The pool of characters used to build CAPTCHAs — letters (a–z, A–Z) and digits (0–9).

field.summary: How long a CAPTCHA stays valid (minutes).
field.usage: The number of minutes a generated CAPTCHA remains valid before it must be refreshed.

field.summary: Assign a customer group automatically from VAT validation.
field.usage: When Yes, customers are placed into a group automatically based on their VAT number validation result, using the group mappings below.

field.summary: Require email confirmation for newly created accounts.
field.usage: When Yes, new accounts must be confirmed through an emailed link before the customer can sign in.

field.summary: The customer group new accounts are assigned to.
field.usage: The default group applied to newly created customer accounts.

field.summary: Email template asking a new customer to confirm their account.
field.usage: The transactional template that carries the account-confirmation link.

field.summary: Email template sent once an account is confirmed.
field.usage: Sent instead of the welcome email after a customer confirms their account.

field.summary: Default domain for the sender of new-account emails.
field.usage: The email domain used in the from-address of account emails — typically the store's domain.

field.summary: The store identity new-account emails are sent from.
field.usage: Which store email identity (sender) is used for account-creation emails.

field.summary: Welcome email for accounts created without a password.
field.usage: Sent instead of the default welcome email when an account is created without a password, so the customer can set one via the link.

field.summary: Require an email address when creating an order in the admin.
field.usage: When Yes, the Email field is mandatory while an admin creates an order.

field.summary: The welcome email template for new accounts.
field.usage: The default transactional template sent when a customer account is created.

field.summary: Generate readable customer increment IDs.
field.usage: When Yes, customers receive human-friendly sequential IDs rather than raw entity IDs.

field.summary: Which address is used for VAT validation at registration.
field.usage: Whether the billing or the shipping address is used when validating a customer's VAT number and assigning a group.

field.summary: Show the VAT Number field on the storefront.
field.usage: When Yes, customers can enter a VAT number on account and address forms.

field.summary: Disable automatic VAT-based group assignment by default.
field.usage: When Yes, automatic group assignment from VAT validation is off unless explicitly enabled.

field.summary: Group for customers with a valid domestic VAT ID.
field.usage: The group assigned when a customer's VAT number is valid and from the store's own country.

field.summary: Group used when VAT validation cannot be completed.
field.usage: The group assigned when the VAT validation service is unavailable or returns an error.

field.summary: Group for customers with a valid intra-EU VAT ID.
field.usage: The group assigned when a customer's VAT number is valid and from another EU country.

field.summary: Group for customers whose VAT ID is invalid.
field.usage: The group assigned when a customer's VAT number fails validation.

field.summary: Re-validate VAT on every order, not just at registration.
field.usage: When Yes, the customer's VAT number is re-checked on each transaction and their group updated accordingly.

field.summary: How long a customer counts as "online" (minutes).
field.usage: The window during which a customer is considered online after their last activity. Leave empty for the default of 15 minutes.

field.summary: How long private customer section data is cached (minutes).
field.usage: The lifetime, in minutes, of the private customer-section data cached in the browser (cart, account state).

field.summary: Allow browser autocomplete on storefront password fields.
field.usage: When Yes, browsers may autofill login and password fields on the storefront.

field.summary: The store identity password-reset emails are sent from.
field.usage: Which store email identity (sender) is used for forgot-password emails.

field.summary: The email template for forgot-password requests.
field.usage: The transactional template carrying the password-reset link.

field.summary: Failed logins before an account is locked.
field.usage: The number of consecutive failed logins that locks a customer account. Use 0 to disable locking.

field.summary: How long a locked account stays locked (minutes).
field.usage: The time, in minutes, after which a locked account is automatically unlocked.

field.summary: Maximum password-reset requests allowed per hour.
field.usage: Caps how many reset requests one account or IP can make each hour. Use 0 to disable the limit.

field.summary: Minimum delay between password-reset requests (minutes).
field.usage: The enforced wait between consecutive reset requests. Use 0 to disable.

field.summary: Minimum number of characters in a customer password.
field.usage: The shortest password a customer may set. Must be 1 or greater.

field.summary: How password-reset requests are rate-limited.
field.usage: Whether reset-request limits are tracked by IP, by email, by both, or not enforced at all.

field.summary: The email template for password reminders.
field.usage: The transactional template used to remind a customer of their password.

field.summary: How many character types a password must include.
field.usage: The number of distinct character classes — lowercase, uppercase, digits, special — a password must contain.

field.summary: How long a password-reset link stays valid (hours).
field.usage: The lifetime of a reset link before it expires. Must be 1 or greater.

field.summary: The email template confirming a password reset.
field.usage: The transactional template sent to confirm a successful password reset.

field.summary: Send customers to their dashboard right after login.
field.usage: When Yes, customers land on their account dashboard after signing in. When No, they stay on the page they were on.

field.summary: Yes also caches custom EAV attributes, not just system ones; speeds loads but needs a cache flush after attribute changes.
field.usage: By default only system EAV attributes are cached (per the note); setting Yes also caches user-defined attributes, speeding attribute loading. Trade-off: after creating or editing custom attributes you may need to flush the cache for changes to show. Default scope.

field.summary: Combines CSS files into fewer requests to speed up page loads.
field.usage: When Yes, the storefront's CSS files are merged into fewer files to reduce HTTP requests. A production performance option. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Combines and shrinks CSS to cut file size and requests; ignored in developer mode.
field.usage: Minifies storefront CSS to reduce file size and speed page loads. As the native note says, it is skipped in developer mode. Can differ per website/store view, and changes take effect after static content is redeployed and caches are flushed.

field.summary: Yes inlines critical CSS and loads the rest asynchronously to speed first render; needs a theme critical.css.
field.usage: When Yes, critical CSS is inlined and the remaining stylesheets load asynchronously, improving first render. As the field note warns, your theme must provide a critical.css file, or styling will be incomplete until the async CSS arrives.

field.summary: Shows the template file path of each block on Admin pages for debugging.
field.usage: When Yes, Admin pages display the path of the .phtml template rendering each block. A development aid; keep No in production.

field.summary: Adds each block's PHP class name alongside the template path hints.
field.usage: When Yes, the template path hints also show the PHP block class that renders each template. Only meaningful while template path hints are enabled. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Secret token added to the URL to switch storefront template hints on; applies only when hints-by-parameter is enabled.
field.usage: The token you append as ?templatehints=<value> to reveal template hints on the storefront. It applies only when storefront template hints and the show-with-parameter option are both enabled, letting developers toggle hints without exposing them to every visitor. Scoped per store view.

field.summary: Shows the template file path of each block on storefront pages for debugging.
field.usage: When Yes, storefront pages are overlaid with the path of the .phtml template rendering each block, to help locate markup. A development aid; keep No in production. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Yes lets developers toggle storefront template hints via a URL parameter instead of for all visitors.
field.usage: With Yes, developers can switch storefront template path hints on per request by adding the URL parameter, instead of showing them to every visitor. Applies only when storefront template hints are enabled, and can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Chooses server- vs client-side style compilation during development; only meaningful outside production mode.
field.usage: Selects how frontend styles are built during development, server-side compilation versus client-side compilation in the browser. As the native note says, it does nothing in production mode where static assets are pre-deployed; it only shapes the workflow in default/developer mode.

field.summary: Whether sales grid data is re-indexed asynchronously in the background.
field.usage: When Enabled, updates to the order, invoice, shipment and credit memo grids are indexed asynchronously by cron rather than on each save, which improves save performance on busy stores. Options are Enable and Disable.

field.summary: Picks the imaging library for catalog images; flush Catalog Images cache or old renders persist.
field.usage: Selects the PHP imaging library used to resize and process catalog images, which affects image quality and generation speed. Already-processed images stay cached, so the storefront keeps serving the old renders until you flush the Catalog Images cache.

field.summary: Yes defers non-critical head scripts to speed first render, but order-dependent inline scripts can break.
field.usage: When Yes, non-critical scripts in the head get a defer attribute so they no longer block page parsing, improving initial render. Those scripts then run later and in a different order, which can break inline code that expects them immediately. Can differ per website/store.

field.summary: Bundles JavaScript modules together to reduce the number of requests.
field.usage: When Yes, JavaScript is bundled for the storefront to cut request count. A production performance option. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Combines JavaScript files into fewer requests to speed up page loads.
field.usage: When Yes, the storefront's JavaScript files are merged into fewer files to reduce HTTP requests. A production performance option. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Yes strips whitespace from JS to shrink downloads and speed the storefront; No serves it unminified. Ignored in developer mode.
field.usage: When Yes, JavaScript files are minified to cut payload size and speed page loads; No serves them unminified for easier debugging. As the native note says, minification is skipped in developer mode, so the effect shows only in default/production mode. Can differ per website/store view.

field.summary: Whether JavaScript is output at the bottom of the page instead of in the head.
field.usage: When Yes, <script> tags are moved to the end of the HTML body so page content can render before scripts load, which can improve perceived load time. Applies globally (default scope).

field.summary: Browser sessionStorage key under which captured client-side JS errors are stored, so developers can read them from the console.
field.usage: Names the browser sessionStorage key where the storefront stashes collected JavaScript errors. Developers read that key in the browser console to retrieve the logged errors when debugging client-side issues.

field.summary: Yes records JS errors in the browser's session storage for test/diagnostic reporting.
field.usage: When Yes, JavaScript errors are captured into the browser's session storage. As the field note says, functional tests can read these for extended reporting; it is a diagnostic aid rather than a storefront feature.

field.summary: How JS string translations are delivered to the browser; changing it requires redeploying static files or storefront JS text breaks.
field.usage: Chooses the mechanism for delivering JavaScript translations to the storefront (for example a translation dictionary versus embedded strings). As the native note warns, switching strategy requires maintenance mode and a static-content redeploy, or client-side translated text will break.

field.summary: Limits developer features (like template hints) to these IPs; empty means no IP restriction.
field.usage: Restricts developer client features to a comma-separated IP allowlist. Leave empty to allow any location per the native note; set it to expose debugging tools only to your own addresses. Website/store scoped.

field.summary: Appends a version to static asset URLs so browsers fetch fresh files after a deploy.
field.usage: When Yes, static files are served with a signature/version in their URL, forcing clients to reload updated assets after each deployment instead of serving stale cached copies.

field.summary: Lets themes load templates through symlinks (handy for linked local packages); on production it's an escape-the-theme-dir security risk.
field.usage: Allowing symlinks lets the template engine follow symlinked paths, convenient when developing with linked packages locally. On production it widens the attack surface: anyone able to place a symlink can make Magento render files outside the theme directory, so keep it No. Scoped per website/store.

field.summary: Strips whitespace from rendered HTML to cut page size; has no effect in developer mode.
field.usage: When Yes, page HTML is minified to reduce transfer size. As the native note says, it is skipped in developer mode, so test it in production mode. Changing it affects cached output — flush the page cache to see the result. Website/store scoped.

field.summary: Enables in-place editing of storefront translations directly on the page.
field.usage: When Yes, translatable strings on the storefront can be edited inline by an authorised user. A translation/development aid; keep No in production. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Yes turns on in-place translation of Admin text; a dev aid only, and heed the note about disabling caches.
field.usage: When Yes, Admin interface strings can be translated inline in the browser — a development aid, not for production. The native note matters: with block/translate output caches on, your edits won't appear until caches are cleared. Default scope only.

field.summary: The countries customers may register and order from.
field.usage: The set of countries offered in address country dropdowns across the store.

field.summary: The country selected by default on address forms.
field.usage: The pre-selected country for new addresses and the default used when guessing a visitor's region.

field.summary: Countries shown at the top of country dropdowns.
field.usage: Priority countries listed first, above a separator, in country selectors for quicker selection.

field.summary: Which countries are treated as part of the EU.
field.usage: The countries Magento considers EU members, used for VAT and tax rules.

field.summary: Countries where the postal code is optional.
field.usage: Countries for which a ZIP / postal code is not required on address forms.

field.summary: The store's language and locale.
field.usage: The locale that sets the storefront language along with date and number formats.

field.summary: The first day of the week in calendars.
field.usage: Which day date pickers and calendars start the week on.

field.summary: The store's time zone.
field.usage: The time zone used for order timestamps, reports and scheduled (cron) tasks.

field.summary: Which days count as the weekend.
field.usage: The days treated as the weekend in sales reports and statistics.

field.summary: The unit used for product weights.
field.usage: Whether product weights are expressed in pounds or kilograms.

field.summary: Show the state/region field for all countries.
field.usage: When Yes, the state/region selector is shown even for countries that have no predefined region list.

field.summary: Countries where a state/region is mandatory.
field.usage: The countries for which customers must provide a state or region on address forms.

field.summary: Hide multi-store controls for a single-store setup.
field.usage: When Yes, store and website scope switchers are hidden to simplify the admin. Ignored if the installation has more than one store.

field.summary: Your business city.
field.usage: The city of your business address, shown on documents.

field.summary: The country your business is located in.
field.usage: Your business country, shown on documents and used in some tax and VAT logic.

field.summary: Your store's opening hours.
field.usage: Business hours shown to customers wherever store information is displayed.

field.summary: Your business VAT number.
field.usage: The merchant VAT number shown on documents and used for EU VAT validation.

field.summary: Your store or company name.
field.usage: The business name shown on invoices, emails and other documents.

field.summary: Your store contact phone number.
field.usage: The phone number shown to customers and on documents.

field.summary: Your business postal code.
field.usage: The postal code of your business address, shown on documents.

field.summary: The state or region your business is in.
field.usage: Your business state/region, shown on documents.

field.summary: Your business street address.
field.usage: The first line of your business street address, shown on documents.

field.summary: Additional business street address line.
field.usage: An optional second line for your business street address.

field.summary: Check your VAT number against the EU service.
field.usage: Validates the merchant VAT number entered above against the EU VIES service.

field.summary: Enables Google AdWords conversion tracking on the storefront.
field.usage: When Yes, the AdWords conversion tracking snippet is added to the order success page. Set to No to remove it. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: Color of the Google AdWords conversion-tracking snippet; applies only when Google AdWords is enabled.
field.usage: Sets the color value used by the Google AdWords conversion-tracking tag. A backend model validates the entered color. Applies only when Enable Google AdWords is set to Yes. Can differ per website and store view.

field.summary: Format of the conversion value reported to Google AdWords conversion tracking.
field.usage: Sets the conversion-value format sent to Google AdWords conversion tracking. Applies only when AdWords is enabled (google/adwords/active). Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: The Google AdWords conversion ID that identifies your account for tracking.
field.usage: The conversion ID issued by Google AdWords, used to attribute storefront conversions to your account. Applies only when Enable is set to Yes. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The Google AdWords conversion label paired with the conversion ID.
field.usage: The conversion label from AdWords that, together with the conversion ID, identifies the specific conversion action being tracked. Applies only when Enable is set to Yes. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The language of the AdWords conversion tracking snippet.
field.usage: Selects the language used by the AdWords conversion tracking code. Applies only when Enable is set to Yes. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The fixed conversion value reported to Google AdWords.
field.usage: The constant value sent with each tracked conversion. Applies only when Enable is Yes and Conversion Value Type is set to a fixed value. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether the tracked conversion value is a fixed amount or taken dynamically from the order.
field.usage: Chooses between reporting a constant conversion value and a value derived from each order. The choice determines whether Conversion Value or Send Order Currency applies. Applies only when Enable is set to Yes.

field.summary: Whether to send the order currency with the dynamic conversion value.
field.usage: When Yes, the order's currency is included alongside the conversion value. Applies only when Enable is Yes and Conversion Value Type uses the dynamic order value. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The Google Analytics measurement/tracking ID that storefront data is sent to.
field.usage: The Google Analytics account identifier (tracking/measurement ID) for the storefront. Applies only when Enable is set to Yes. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Enables Google Analytics tracking on the storefront.
field.usage: When Yes, the Google Analytics tracking script is added to storefront pages. Can be configured per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether visitor IP addresses are anonymized before being sent to Google Analytics.
field.usage: When Yes, visitor IP addresses are anonymized before being sent to Google Analytics, which helps with privacy compliance. Applies only when Enable is Yes.

field.summary: Enables Google Content Experiments (A/B testing) integration for the storefront.
field.usage: When Yes, Google Content Experiments code is injected for A/B testing. Applies only when the associated Google Analytics integration is enabled. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Turns on Google Ads (AdWords) conversion tracking.
field.usage: When Yes, Google Ads conversion tracking is added to the storefront via gtag.js. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Google Ads conversion ID for gtag tracking; applies only when AdWords is active. Can differ per store view.
field.usage: The Google Ads conversion ID (the field note shows the AW-XXXXXXXX form) that the gtag conversion tag reports against. Applies only when Google AdWords tracking is active, and is scoped to website/store so each view can report to its own account.

field.summary: The Google Ads conversion label reported when a conversion occurs.
field.usage: The conversion label from your Google Ads account, used to attribute conversions. Applies only when Google AdWords tracking is enabled. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Turns on Google Analytics 4 tracking via gtag.js.
field.usage: When Yes, the storefront loads Google Analytics 4 tracking through gtag.js. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Enables Google Content Experiments (A/B testing) integration for Google Analytics 4.
field.usage: When Yes, Google Content Experiments code is injected for A/B testing under the Google Analytics 4 integration. Applies only when Google Analytics 4 is enabled. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: GA4 Measurement ID tying tracking tags to your Analytics property; must match or no data lands.
field.usage: The GA4 Measurement ID (G-XXXXXXXX) linking storefront tracking tags to your Google Analytics property; it must match that property or no data is recorded. Applies only when the integration is active, and can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Yes disables page cache during Login-as-Customer so personalized pages aren't served to others.
field.usage: Yes turns off full-page cache while an admin is logged in as a customer, so the impersonated session's personalized pages are not cached and later served to real shoppers. It trades some performance during the session for that safety.

field.summary: Turns the Login as Customer feature on or off for admin users.
field.usage: When Yes, administrators can open the storefront as a customer to troubleshoot or assist with their account. Set to No to disable the feature entirely.

field.summary: The label shown next to the customer opt-in checkbox for Login as Customer assistance.
field.usage: The text displayed beside the opt-in checkbox customers use to allow store staff to sign in as them (Login as Customer). Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: The tooltip text explaining the Login as Customer opt-in checkbox to customers.
field.usage: The tooltip shown with the Login as Customer opt-in checkbox, explaining to customers what granting assistance permission means. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: Which store view a Login-as-Customer session opens in.
field.usage: Controls which store view the admin's Login-as-Customer session starts in. As the native note explains, choose Manual Selection on multi-website setups that share customer accounts so the admin picks the store after logging in; otherwise the store is resolved automatically.

field.summary: Contact URL published in your security.txt file; must be an https address.
field.usage: The contact page advertised in security.txt for reporting vulnerabilities. It must be a valid secure (https) URL, which the backend enforces. Website scoped.

field.summary: The security contact email address published in security.txt.
field.usage: The email address researchers should use to report security issues; it is listed as a Contact entry in the published security.txt. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The security contact phone number published in security.txt.
field.usage: A phone number researchers can use to report security issues; it is listed as a Contact entry in the published security.txt. Can differ per website.

field.summary: Turns the published security.txt file on or off.
field.usage: When set to Yes, the store publishes a security.txt file (under /.well-known/) describing how security researchers should report issues. Can be set per website.

field.summary: HTTPS URL published in security.txt crediting security researchers (e.g. a hall-of-fame page).
field.usage: The Acknowledgements URL written into your site's security.txt, typically linking to a page thanking security researchers (native example). Must be a secure (HTTPS) URL, enforced by the backend model. Can differ per website.

field.summary: HTTPS URL to your PGP key, published in security.txt so researchers can encrypt vulnerability reports.
field.usage: The URL published in your site's security.txt that points to a PGP key (e.g. https://example.com/pgp-key.txt, per the note), letting security researchers encrypt the vulnerability reports they send you. Must be an https address. Set per website.

field.summary: Optional https URL in security.txt pointing to security-related job openings.
field.usage: Optional URL published in the site's security.txt file to point security researchers at relevant job openings. Must be an https URL. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The URL of your security policy, published in security.txt; must be a secure (HTTPS) URL.
field.usage: The address of your vulnerability-disclosure or security policy page, published as the Policy entry in security.txt. The value must be a secure (HTTPS) URL. Can differ per website.

field.summary: Fills the Preferred-Languages field of your published security.txt, signalling which languages your team reads.
field.usage: Populates the Preferred-Languages field of the published security.txt file, telling security researchers which languages your team can handle reports in. Enter comma-separated language codes (e.g. en, es, de). Can differ per website.

field.summary: The signature used to sign the published security.txt file.
field.usage: Optional signature text associated with the security.txt file, letting researchers verify its authenticity. Can differ per website.

field.summary: Shows or hides the inline documentation markers next to config fields.
field.usage: When Yes, a documentation marker appears beside each configuration field that has a note; No hides all markers. The notes are bundled with the module, so toggling this changes only the admin UI and fetches nothing externally.

field.summary: Adds a "Full documentation" link to any inline note that carries a URL.
field.usage: Beyond the native note: this applies only when Inline Documentation is enabled (its dependency), and affects every config note that defines a documentation URL — notes without a URL are untouched. Set once globally.

field.summary: Whether customers can ship a single order to multiple addresses.
field.usage: When Yes, customers can split an order across several shipping addresses during checkout; when No, each order ships to one address. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The maximum item quantity allowed when shipping to multiple addresses.
field.usage: Caps the total quantity of items a customer may ship across multiple addresses in one order. Applies only when Allow Shipping to Multiple Addresses is set to Yes. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Enables the scheduled job that reports data to New Relic.
field.usage: When Yes, the cron job that collects and sends reporting data to New Relic runs on its schedule; No stops it. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: The New Relic account reporting data is sent to; must match your license/key account or nothing shows up.
field.usage: The New Relic account ID that Magento's reporting data is sent to. It must correspond to the account tied to your New Relic license and API key, or data won't appear in the dashboards. Applies only when New Relic reporting is enabled. Set per website or store view.

field.summary: New Relic API key used to post deployment markers and reporting data; applies only when New Relic reporting is on. Stored encrypted; per website/store.
field.usage: The New Relic API key Magento uses to post deployment markers and reporting data. Applies only when New Relic reporting is enabled; find it under Events then Deployments in New Relic APM. Stored encrypted and settable per website/store.

field.summary: Selects the New Relic API used for reporting: legacy v2 REST or the current NerdGraph (GraphQL).
field.usage: Chooses how Magento talks to New Relic: the legacy v2 REST API or the modern NerdGraph (GraphQL) interface (native note). Prefer NerdGraph for current accounts; v2 suits older setups still on that API. Applies only when New Relic reporting is enabled (depends). Can differ per website/store view.

field.summary: Legacy v2 REST endpoint for New Relic deployment markers; needs reporting on and v2 REST mode.
field.usage: The endpoint Magento posts New Relic deployment markers to, using the legacy v2 REST API. Applies only when New Relic reporting is enabled and the API mode is set to v2 REST. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: New Relic application ID data is reported to; applies only when New Relic reporting is enabled. Can differ per store view.
field.usage: The numeric New Relic application ID the module reports to; the field note explains it sits in the APM URL after /applications/. Applies only when New Relic reporting is enabled, and is scoped to website/store.

field.summary: Must match your New Relic app name so Magento data lands in the right APM app; used only when enabled.
field.usage: Application name Magento reports under; it must match the app configured in New Relic so data lands in the correct APM application. Applies only when New Relic reporting is enabled. Can differ per website/store.

field.summary: Turns the New Relic reporting integration on or off.
field.usage: When Yes, the New Relic reporting integration is active; No disables it. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: New Relic entity GUID for NerdGraph; leave empty to auto-detect from the App ID.
field.usage: Identifies the New Relic entity that receives data via NerdGraph. Applies only when New Relic reporting is enabled and the API mode is NerdGraph. Leave empty to auto-detect from the App ID. Can differ per website/store view.

field.summary: Endpoint Magento posts New Relic Insights events to; %s is replaced with the account ID.
field.usage: The URL events are sent to for New Relic Insights reporting, with %s substituted by your account ID per the native note. Applies only when New Relic reporting is enabled. Website/store scoped.

field.summary: The New Relic Insights insert key that authorizes Magento to push event/metric data; stored encrypted.
field.usage: The Insights insert key used to authenticate Magento when it sends custom event and metric data to New Relic. Generate it under Insights → API Keys → Insert Keys (native note); stored encrypted. Used only when reporting is enabled (depends). Can differ per website/store view.

field.summary: Endpoint deployment markers are sent to; only used when New Relic is on and in NerdGraph mode.
field.usage: NerdGraph API endpoint that deployment events are reported to (recommended). Used only when New Relic reporting is enabled and the API mode is NerdGraph. Can differ per website/store.

field.summary: Also reports each Magento area (adminhtml, frontend...) as its own New Relic app.
field.usage: In addition to the main app, creates a separate New Relic app per Magento area code so each can be monitored on its own. Applies only when reporting is enabled and requires the New Relic application name to be set. More granularity means more NR apps to manage.

field.summary: Turns the newsletter subscription feature on or off.
field.usage: Controls whether newsletter functionality is available, including the storefront subscription form. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether visitors without an account can subscribe to the newsletter.
field.usage: When Yes, guests who are not registered customers can sign up for the newsletter; when No, only registered customers can subscribe. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Whether subscribers must confirm via an email link (double opt-in) before being subscribed.
field.usage: When Yes, newsletter sign-ups use double opt-in: a confirmation email is sent and the subscription becomes active only once the link is clicked. Can be set per store view.

field.summary: Which store email identity the newsletter confirmation email is sent from.
field.usage: Selects the sender identity for the subscription confirmation (double opt-in) email — one of the Store Email Addresses identities (General Contact, Sales Representative, Customer Support, Custom 1/2). Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Template for the newsletter double opt-in confirmation email; Default follows theme fallback.
field.usage: The template for the confirmation (double opt-in) email sent when a visitor subscribes to the newsletter. Default follows theme fallback; a custom template overrides it. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Which store email identity the newsletter subscription-success email is sent from.
field.usage: Selects the sender identity for the email confirming a successful newsletter subscription — one of the Store Email Addresses identities. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Template for the newsletter subscription-success email; can differ per store view.
field.usage: The email template sent to confirm a successful newsletter subscription. As the field note says, Default resolves through theme fallback. Scoped to website/store, so each store view can confirm with its own template.

field.summary: Which store email identity the newsletter unsubscribe email is sent from.
field.usage: Selects the sender identity for the email sent when a customer unsubscribes from the newsletter — one of the Store Email Addresses identities. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Template for the email confirming a newsletter unsubscription; 'Default' resolves via theme fallback. Per website/store.
field.usage: The email template sent to confirm that someone has unsubscribed from the newsletter. 'Default' resolves through theme fallback. Can differ per website/store view.

field.summary: Hours an admin OAuth token stays valid; empty disables expiry.
field.usage: How many hours an admin integration OAuth token remains valid before expiring. Shorter lifetimes limit the damage from a leaked token; as the native note says, leaving it empty turns expiry off so tokens never lapse.

field.summary: How long a customer API token stays valid; shorter is safer, empty means tokens never expire.
field.usage: Validity period, in hours, for customer REST/OAuth access tokens. Shorter lifetimes limit exposure if a token leaks but force customers to re-authenticate sooner; leaving it empty disables expiry so tokens never time out.

field.summary: Number of failed OAuth/API logins before the account is locked, throttling brute-force attempts; lower is stricter.
field.usage: The count of consecutive authentication failures allowed before the OAuth/API account is locked out, limiting brute-force attacks. Lower values are stricter but risk locking legitimate integrations after a few mistakes. Global setting (default scope).

field.summary: How long an account stays locked after too many failed OAuth attempts; longer slows brute-force attacks.
field.usage: Time, in seconds, an account stays locked once it hits the failed-authentication threshold before it unlocks automatically. Longer periods slow brute-force attempts but can inconvenience legitimate users who mistype.

field.summary: Runs token cleanup on about 1 in X OAuth requests; lower cleans more often, 0 disables it.
field.usage: A probabilistic trigger: roughly one in every X OAuth requests also runs token cleanup. A lower number cleans up more often with slightly more overhead per request; 0 disables cleanup and lets expired tokens accumulate (not recommended).

field.summary: How long, in minutes, expired OAuth entries are retained before cleanup removes them.
field.usage: The age, in minutes as the field note says, past which expired OAuth tokens and nonces are purged by the cleanup routine. A shorter period keeps the OAuth tables lean; too short could remove entries still useful for debugging.

field.summary: Whether an integration's OAuth access token can be used directly as a standalone Bearer token in API requests.
field.usage: When set to Yes, an integration's OAuth access token can be passed as a standalone Bearer token to authenticate Web API requests, instead of signing each call with the full OAuth 1.0a flow. Found under OAuth → Consumer Settings.

field.summary: Seconds allowed to finish the OAuth handshake before the consumer key/secret expire; shorter is safer but can break slow integrations.
field.usage: The window, in seconds, in which an OAuth handshake must complete after token exchange begins before the consumer key/secret expire unused. A short window limits how long a leaked key is usable; too short can break integrations that authorize slowly.

field.summary: How many HTTP redirects the OAuth consumer-credentials POST will follow.
field.usage: Maximum redirects followed when posting OAuth consumer credentials to the integration endpoint. Raise it if the endpoint legitimately redirects; keep it low to avoid chasing unexpected hops. Default scope only.

field.summary: Seconds Magento waits for the remote endpoint when posting OAuth consumer credentials; too low fails on slow endpoints.
field.usage: How many seconds Magento waits for a response when posting OAuth consumer credentials to an integration's endpoint during setup. Set too low, the handshake fails against slow endpoints; too high, a stuck request ties things up longer. Default scope.

field.summary: The merchant country used to decide which payment solutions are offered.
field.usage: Your business's country. Payment providers such as PayPal use it to decide which solutions are available. Defaults to the store's general country when left unset.

field.summary: Your PayPal-issued publisher ID that identifies the account the PayPal Credit advertising banner is served for.
field.usage: The publisher identifier PayPal issues for the Advertise PayPal Credit program. It must be supplied for the credit banner to render; without it no banner is displayed. Enter the value from your PayPal account rather than guessing. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Whether the PayPal Pay Later banner is shown on the storefront category page.
field.usage: Turns the PayPal Pay Later (Bill Me Later) promotional banner on or off on the category page. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Placement of the PayPal Pay Later (BML) banner on catalog category pages.
field.usage: Chooses where the Pay Later / Bill Me Later promotional banner appears on catalog category pages. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Size of the PayPal Credit (Bill Me Later) banner shown on catalog category pages.
field.usage: Chooses the display size of the PayPal Credit / Bill Me Later promotional banner on the Catalog Category Page, from the available banner sizes. Applies only for the configured category-page banner position, and can be set per website.

field.summary: Size of the PayPal Credit (Bill Me Later) banner shown on catalog category pages.
field.usage: Chooses the display size of the PayPal Credit / Bill Me Later promotional banner on the Catalog Category Page, from the available banner sizes. Applies only for the configured category-page banner position, and can be set per website.

field.summary: Shows the PayPal Bill Me Later promotional banner on the shopping cart page.
field.usage: When Yes, the PayPal Bill Me Later (PayPal Credit) banner appears on the shopping cart page; No hides it.

field.summary: Placement of the PayPal Credit (BML) banner on the checkout shopping cart page.
field.usage: Chooses where the PayPal Credit (Pay Later/BML) advertising banner appears on the checkout cart page. The available placements come from PayPal's banner position options. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Display size of the PayPal Credit (BML) banner on the shopping cart page.
field.usage: Sets the size of the PayPal Credit / Banner-based-lending promo banner shown on the Checkout Cart Page. Applies only when the cart-page banner's Position is set to the matching layout option. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Display size of the PayPal Credit (BML) banner on the shopping cart page.
field.usage: Sets the size of the PayPal Credit / Banner-based-lending promo banner shown on the Checkout Cart Page. Applies only when the cart-page banner's Position is set to the matching layout option. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Whether the PayPal Pay Later banner is shown on the storefront home page.
field.usage: Turns the PayPal Pay Later (Bill Me Later) promotional banner on or off on the home page. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Placement of the PayPal Pay Later (BML) banner on the storefront home page.
field.usage: Chooses where the Pay Later / Bill Me Later promotional banner appears on the home page. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Size of the PayPal Credit (Bill Me Later) banner shown on the home page.
field.usage: Chooses the display size of the PayPal Credit / Bill Me Later promotional banner on the Home Page, from the available banner sizes. Applies only for the configured home-page banner position, and can be set per website.

field.summary: Size of the PayPal Credit (Bill Me Later) banner shown on the home page.
field.usage: Chooses the display size of the PayPal Credit / Bill Me Later promotional banner on the Home Page, from the available banner sizes. Applies only for the configured home-page banner position, and can be set per website.

field.summary: Shows the PayPal Bill Me Later promotional banner on catalog product pages.
field.usage: When Yes, the PayPal Bill Me Later (PayPal Credit) banner appears on catalog product pages; No hides it.

field.summary: Placement of the PayPal Credit (BML) banner on the catalog product page.
field.usage: Chooses where the PayPal Credit (Pay Later/BML) advertising banner appears on product detail pages. Placements come from PayPal's banner position options. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Display size of the PayPal Credit (BML) banner on the product page.
field.usage: Sets the size of the PayPal Credit / Banner-based-lending promo banner shown on the Catalog Product Page. Applies only when the product-page banner's Position is set to the matching layout option. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Display size of the PayPal Credit (BML) banner on the product page.
field.usage: Sets the size of the PayPal Credit / Banner-based-lending promo banner shown on the Catalog Product Page. Applies only when the product-page banner's Position is set to the matching layout option. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Turns PayPal Pay Later promotional banners on or off across the storefront.
field.usage: Master switch for advertising PayPal Pay Later messaging. When Yes, the Pay Later banners configured for each page are eligible to show. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Color of the PayPal Pay Later banner on the shopping cart page.
field.usage: Selects the color variant of the Pay Later banner shown on the cart page. Applies only when the cart-page Pay Later banner is displayed and its style layout is set to flex. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Whether the PayPal Pay Later message is shown on the shopping cart page.
field.usage: When Yes, the PayPal Pay Later promotional message appears on the Checkout Cart Page; when No, it is hidden. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Placement of the logo within the PayPal Pay Later banner on the cart page.
field.usage: Sets where the logo sits inside the Pay Later messaging banner on the shopping cart page. Applies only when the cart-page Pay Later banner is displayed with a text style layout.

field.summary: Logo variant for the PayPal Pay Later message on the shopping cart page.
field.usage: Selects which PayPal Pay Later logo style is shown in the cart-page message. Applies only when the cart-page Pay Later message is displayed and its style layout is set to text. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Where the PayPal Pay Later banner is placed on the shopping cart page.
field.usage: Chooses the placement of the Pay Later banner on the Checkout Cart Page from the available positions. Applies only when the cart-page Pay Later banner Display is enabled. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Aspect ratio of the flex-layout PayPal Pay Later banner on the shopping cart page.
field.usage: Chooses the aspect ratio/size of the flex-layout PayPal Pay Later banner on the cart page. Applies only when that banner is displayed and its style layout is flex. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Layout style of the PayPal Pay Later banner on the shopping cart page.
field.usage: Selects the layout style of the Pay Later banner on the cart page. Applies only when the cart-page Pay Later banner is displayed. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Text color of the PayPal Pay Later message on the cart page.
field.usage: Selects the text color of the PayPal Pay Later message on the Checkout Cart Page, from the available color options. Applies only when the cart-page Pay Later message is enabled and its style layout is set to Text. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Text size of the PayPal Pay Later banner on the cart page.
field.usage: Sets the size of the message text in the Pay Later banner on the shopping cart page. Applies only when the cart-page Pay Later banner is displayed with a text style layout.

field.summary: Color scheme for the PayPal Pay Later message on catalog category pages.
field.usage: Selects the color scheme of the PayPal Pay Later banner shown on catalog category pages. Applies only when the category-page Pay Later message is displayed and its style layout is set to flex. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Whether the PayPal Pay Later banner is shown on category pages.
field.usage: When Yes, the PayPal Pay Later promotional banner appears on the Catalog Category Page; when No, it is hidden. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Position of the PayPal logo within the Pay Later text banner on the category page.
field.usage: Where the PayPal logo sits within the text-layout Pay Later banner on the category page. Applies only when that banner is displayed with a text style layout and a primary/alternative logo type. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Logo style of the PayPal Pay Later banner on catalog category pages.
field.usage: Selects the logo style of the Pay Later banner on category pages. Applies only when the category-page Pay Later banner is displayed and its style layout is set to text. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Placement of the PayPal Pay Later message on catalog category pages.
field.usage: Chooses where the PayPal Pay Later message is placed on the Catalog Category Page, from the available positions. Applies only when the category-page Pay Later message is enabled. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Aspect ratio of the PayPal Pay Later banner on category pages.
field.usage: Sets the shape/aspect ratio of the Pay Later banner on catalog category pages. Applies only when the category-page Pay Later banner is displayed with a flex style layout.

field.summary: Layout style of the PayPal Pay Later message on catalog category pages.
field.usage: Chooses the layout format of the PayPal Pay Later banner on catalog category pages, which in turn determines whether a logo-type or color option applies. Applies only when the category-page Pay Later message is displayed. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Text color of the Pay Later banner on category pages.
field.usage: Selects the text color for the Pay Later banner on the Catalog Category Page from PayPal's allowed color options. Applies only when the category-page banner Display is enabled and its style layout is Text. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Text size of the PayPal Pay Later text banner on the category page.
field.usage: Sets the text size of the text-layout PayPal Pay Later banner on the category page. Applies only when that banner is displayed with a text style layout. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Color of the PayPal Pay Later banner on the checkout payment step.
field.usage: Selects the color variant of the Pay Later banner shown on the checkout payment step. Applies only when that banner is displayed and its style layout is set to flex. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Whether the PayPal Pay Later message is shown at the checkout payment step.
field.usage: When Yes, the PayPal Pay Later promotional message appears at the Checkout Payment Step; when No, it is hidden. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Placement of the logo within the PayPal Pay Later banner at the checkout payment step.
field.usage: Sets where the logo sits inside the Pay Later banner on the checkout payment step. Applies only when that Pay Later banner is displayed with a text style layout.

field.summary: Logo variant for the PayPal Pay Later message on the checkout payment step.
field.usage: Selects which PayPal Pay Later logo style is shown during the checkout payment step. Applies only when that Pay Later message is displayed and its style layout is set to text. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Where the PayPal Pay Later banner is placed at the checkout payment step.
field.usage: Chooses the placement of the Pay Later banner on the Checkout Payment Step from the available positions. Applies only when the payment-step Pay Later banner Display is enabled. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Aspect ratio of the flex-layout PayPal Pay Later banner on the checkout payment step.
field.usage: Chooses the aspect ratio/size of the flex-layout PayPal Pay Later banner on the checkout payment step. Applies only when that banner is displayed and its style layout is flex. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Layout style of the PayPal Pay Later banner on the checkout payment step.
field.usage: Selects the layout style of the Pay Later banner on the checkout payment step. Applies only when that banner is displayed. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Text color of the PayPal Pay Later message at the checkout payment step.
field.usage: Selects the text color of the PayPal Pay Later message at the Checkout Payment Step, from the available color options. Applies only when that message is enabled and its style layout is set to Text. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Text size of the PayPal Pay Later banner at the checkout payment step.
field.usage: Sets the size of the message text in the Pay Later banner on the checkout payment step. Applies only when that Pay Later banner is displayed with a text style layout.

field.summary: Color scheme for the PayPal Pay Later message on the home page.
field.usage: Selects the color scheme of the PayPal Pay Later banner shown on the storefront home page. Applies only when the home-page Pay Later message is displayed and its style layout is set to flex. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Whether the PayPal Pay Later banner is shown on the home page.
field.usage: When Yes, the PayPal Pay Later promotional banner appears on the Home Page; when No, it is hidden. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Position of the PayPal logo within the Pay Later text banner on the home page.
field.usage: Where the PayPal logo sits within the text-layout Pay Later banner on the home page. Applies only when that banner is displayed with a text style layout and a primary/alternative logo type. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Logo style of the PayPal Pay Later banner on the storefront home page.
field.usage: Selects the logo style of the Pay Later banner on the home page. Applies only when the home-page Pay Later banner is displayed and its style layout is set to text. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Placement of the PayPal Pay Later message on the home page.
field.usage: Chooses where the PayPal Pay Later message is placed on the Home Page, from the available positions. Applies only when the home-page Pay Later message is enabled. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Aspect ratio of the PayPal Pay Later banner on the home page.
field.usage: Sets the shape/aspect ratio of the Pay Later banner on the home page. Applies only when the home-page Pay Later banner is displayed with a flex style layout.

field.summary: Layout style of the PayPal Pay Later message on the home page.
field.usage: Chooses the layout format of the PayPal Pay Later banner on the home page. Applies only when the home-page Pay Later message is displayed. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Text color of the Pay Later banner on the home page.
field.usage: Selects the text color for the Pay Later banner on the Home Page from PayPal's allowed color options. Applies only when the home-page banner Display is enabled and its style layout is Text. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Text size of the PayPal Pay Later text banner on the home page.
field.usage: Sets the text size of the text-layout PayPal Pay Later banner on the home page. Applies only when that banner is displayed with a text style layout. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Color of the PayPal Pay Later banner on product detail pages.
field.usage: Selects the color variant of the Pay Later banner shown on product pages. Applies only when that banner is displayed and its style layout is set to flex. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Whether the PayPal Pay Later message is shown on product detail pages.
field.usage: When Yes, the PayPal Pay Later promotional message appears on the Catalog Product Page; when No, it is hidden. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Placement of the logo within the PayPal Pay Later banner on product pages.
field.usage: Sets where the logo sits inside the Pay Later banner on catalog product pages. Applies only when the product-page Pay Later banner is displayed with a text style layout.

field.summary: Logo variant for the PayPal Pay Later message on product pages.
field.usage: Selects which PayPal Pay Later logo style is shown in the product-page message. Applies only when the product-page Pay Later message is displayed and its style layout is set to text. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Where the PayPal Pay Later banner is placed on product pages.
field.usage: Chooses the placement of the Pay Later banner on the Catalog Product Page from the available positions. Applies only when the product-page Pay Later banner Display is enabled. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Aspect ratio of the flex-layout PayPal Pay Later banner on the product page.
field.usage: Chooses the aspect ratio/size of the flex-layout PayPal Pay Later banner on the catalog product page. Applies only when that banner is displayed and its style layout is flex. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Layout style of the PayPal Pay Later banner on product detail pages.
field.usage: Selects the layout style of the Pay Later banner on product pages. Applies only when the product-page Pay Later banner is displayed. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Text color of the PayPal Pay Later message on product detail pages.
field.usage: Selects the text color of the PayPal Pay Later message on the Catalog Product Page, from the available color options. Applies only when the product-page message is enabled and its style layout is set to Text. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Text size of the PayPal Pay Later banner on product pages.
field.usage: Sets the size of the message text in the Pay Later banner on catalog product pages. Applies only when the product-page Pay Later banner is displayed with a text style layout.

field.summary: Enables the PayPal Express Checkout payment solution.
field.usage: Turns PayPal Express Checkout on or off (Yes/No). Can be set per website.

field.summary: Yes adds the PayPal Credit (financing) button to Express Checkout.
field.usage: Turns the PayPal Credit financing option on or off for Express Checkout. When Yes, an integrated button lets eligible buyers pay over time while you are paid up front; it still only appears to buyers PayPal deems eligible.

field.summary: Whether PayPal Express login opens in an on-site overlay instead of redirecting.
field.usage: When Yes, the buyer completes PayPal login and approval in an in-context overlay on your storefront rather than being redirected to PayPal's site; No uses the full-page redirect. Set per website.

field.summary: Enables or disables the PayPal Pay Later experience.
field.usage: Turns the PayPal Pay Later experience on or off for this PayPal solution. When No, Pay Later messaging and banners are not offered. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Display order of PayPal Credit relative to other payment methods at checkout.
field.usage: Sets the position of PayPal Credit among the available payment methods at checkout (lower numbers appear first). Applies only when Express Checkout PayPal Credit is enabled.

field.summary: The method used to authenticate Magento's calls to the PayPal API.
field.usage: Selects how the store authenticates to PayPal's API for Express Checkout (for example, by the type of API credential used). Can be set per website.

field.summary: API certificate file used to authenticate the store's PayPal account for Express Checkout.
field.usage: Uploads the PayPal API certificate that identifies and authenticates the merchant's PayPal account for Express Checkout API calls. Used instead of API signature credentials when certificate authentication is selected. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Password that authenticates Express Checkout API calls to the merchant's PayPal account.
field.usage: The API password used to authenticate Express Checkout API requests against the merchant's PayPal account. Stored encrypted, and can differ per website.

field.summary: API signature credential used to authenticate the store with your PayPal account.
field.usage: The PayPal API signature that authenticates requests from the store to your PayPal account. Stored encrypted. Applies when API signature authentication is in use. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The PayPal API username that identifies the merchant's account for Express Checkout.
field.usage: The API username used to identify and authenticate the merchant's PayPal account for Express Checkout API calls. Stored encrypted. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The email address of the PayPal merchant account that will receive payments.
field.usage: The email tied to your PayPal merchant (business) account — the address payments are credited to. Optional on this screen; PayPal can also be set up via the API credentials instead. Can be set per website for stores that bill under different PayPal accounts.

field.summary: Country used to simulate the buyer's location when testing Express Checkout in sandbox mode.
field.usage: Selects a buyer country, from the country list, to emulate during sandbox testing of PayPal Express Checkout. Applies only when sandbox mode is enabled. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Hostname or IP of the proxy server used for PayPal API calls.
field.usage: The proxy host that PayPal API requests are routed through. Applies only when Use Proxy is enabled. Can be set per website.

field.summary: TCP port of the proxy server used for PayPal API calls.
field.usage: The port on the proxy host that PayPal API requests are routed through. Applies only when Use Proxy is enabled. Valid range is 0–65535. Website-scoped.

field.summary: Whether Express Checkout runs against the PayPal sandbox instead of the live environment.
field.usage: When Yes, Express Checkout uses the PayPal sandbox for testing; when No, it processes live transactions. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Whether PayPal API calls are routed through a proxy server.
field.usage: When Yes, Express Checkout API requests are sent through a proxy host; No connects to PayPal directly.

field.summary: Merchant Account ID that identifies your PayPal account for In-Context Checkout.
field.usage: Your PayPal merchant account identifier, used to associate the store with your PayPal account. Applies only when In-Context Checkout is enabled. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Days a PayPal order authorization stays honored; must match your PayPal account setting.
field.usage: The authorization honor period (in days) that PayPal guarantees funds for an order authorization. Applies only when Payment Action is Order, and it must mirror the value configured on your PayPal account. Website scope.

field.summary: How many child authorizations PayPal may create under one order authorization; the account default is 1.
field.usage: Number of child (partial) authorizations allowed against a single PayPal order authorization. The PayPal account default is 1; raising it requires PayPal to increase your limit. Applies only when the Express Checkout payment action is Order. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Days a PayPal order authorization stays valid; must match your PayPal account setting.
field.usage: Number of days the order remains valid, mirroring the Order Valid Period on your PayPal account — keep the two in sync. Applies only when Payment Action is Order. Can be set per website.

field.summary: The payment action used when an order is placed through PayPal Express Checkout.
field.usage: Selects how a PayPal Express Checkout order is processed at placement — the payment action applied to the transaction. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Whether a billing agreement is created when the buyer has no active one.
field.usage: Controls creation of a PayPal billing agreement during Express Checkout when the buyer has no active agreement. Billing agreements let a customer pay with PayPal later without re-authorising. The choice is a defined set of signup behaviours; set per website.

field.summary: Whether PayPal Express Checkout applies to all allowed countries or only specific ones.
field.usage: Chooses whether PayPal Express Checkout is offered to all allowed countries or only to a specific list of countries (set in the related country field). Can be set per website.

field.summary: Visual style of the PayPal Express Checkout shortcut buttons.
field.usage: Selects the visual flavor of the PayPal shortcut (Express Checkout) buttons shown in the storefront. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether PayPal Express Checkout API calls are logged for debugging.
field.usage: When Yes, requests and responses exchanged with PayPal for Express Checkout are written to the debug log. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Enables the PayPal Billing Agreement payment option at checkout.
field.usage: Turns the PayPal Billing Agreement method on or off. As the native note says, it surfaces at checkout only for customers who already hold at least one active billing agreement, letting them pay without re-entering PayPal each time. Can differ per website.

field.summary: Whether customers can create a PayPal billing agreement from their account.
field.usage: When Yes, customers can set up a PayPal billing agreement through the wizard in their account area; No disables it.

field.summary: Whether the PayPal Billing Agreement method is offered to all countries or only selected ones.
field.usage: Chooses whether PayPal Billing Agreement is available from all allowed countries or only a specific list. When restricted, the countries are chosen in a separate setting. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Logs PayPal API request and response data for Billing Agreement troubleshooting.
field.usage: When Yes, PayPal Billing Agreement API calls are logged to help with troubleshooting; when No, logging is off. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Whether individual cart line items are sent to PayPal for billing-agreement orders.
field.usage: When Yes, each cart line item (name, quantity, price) is transferred to PayPal rather than only the order total, for PayPal Billing Agreement transactions. Can be set per website.

field.summary: How PayPal processes payment for billing-agreement orders.
field.usage: Selects the payment action PayPal performs for billing-agreement orders — for example, authorizing the amount only, or authorizing and capturing it. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Display order of PayPal Billing Agreement among payment methods at checkout.
field.usage: Sets the position of the PayPal Billing Agreement method relative to other payment methods at checkout; lower values appear first. Can be set per website and per store view.

field.summary: Countries whose buyers may use the PayPal billing agreement method.
field.usage: Restricts the PayPal billing agreement method to buyers from the selected countries. Applies only when payment is limited to specific countries.

field.summary: Checkout method name shown to customers for PayPal Billing Agreement.
field.usage: The label displayed to customers for the PayPal Billing Agreement payment method at checkout. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Whether SSL/TLS peer verification is enforced on Billing Agreement API connections.
field.usage: When Yes, the SSL certificate of PayPal's endpoint is verified on Billing Agreement API connections; when No, verification is skipped. Can be set per website.

field.summary: Brazil installment period shown on the PayPal button on the cart page.
field.usage: Selects the Brazil installment period displayed on the PayPal Smart Button when the cart-page button label is set to installment. The option list is PayPal-specific. Can be set per store view.

field.summary: Color of the customized PayPal Credit button on the cart page.
field.usage: Selects the color of the PayPal button on the cart page. Applies only when button customization is enabled and the button label is set to Credit. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether the PayPal smart button on the cart page uses custom styling.
field.usage: When Yes, the PayPal button on the Cart Page uses the custom appearance settings; when No, it uses PayPal's defaults. Can be set per website and per store view.

field.summary: Chooses the label text shown on the PayPal button on the cart page.
field.usage: Selects which label the PayPal Express button displays on the shopping-cart page. Applies only when cart-page button customization is turned on. Scoped per website and store view.

field.summary: Visual layout of the PayPal checkout button on the cart page.
field.usage: Chooses the layout style of the PayPal smart button on the shopping cart page. Applies only when button customization is enabled for the cart page, and can be set per store view.

field.summary: Installment period shown on the Mexico PayPal installments button on the cart page.
field.usage: Selects the installment period offered for the Mexico-specific PayPal installments button on the cart page. Applies only when the cart-page button is customized with the installment label. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Shape of the PayPal smart button on the cart page.
field.usage: Chooses the shape of the PayPal smart payment button shown on the cart page, from PayPal's available button shapes. Applies only when button customization is enabled for the checkout and cart pages. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: Installment period shown on the Brazil installment PayPal button at checkout.
field.usage: Selects the installment period for the Brazil installment button on the checkout page. Applies only when button customization is enabled and the button label is set to Installment. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: Color of the PayPal smart button on the checkout page.
field.usage: Chooses the color of the PayPal button shown on the Checkout Page, from the available button colors. Applies only when button customization is enabled for that location. Can be set per website and per store view.

field.summary: Whether to customize the PayPal button's appearance on the checkout page.
field.usage: When Yes, you can override the default style of the PayPal button on the checkout page; No keeps the defaults. Can be set per store view.

field.summary: Text/label variant shown on the PayPal button on the checkout page; applies only when button customization is on.
field.usage: Chooses which label the PayPal smart button shows on the checkout page (for example a standard pay label or an installment/credit label). Applies only when the checkout-page button is set to be customized. The installment label is available only in the locales en_MX, es_MX, en_BR and pt_BR. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Layout of the PayPal Credit smart button on the checkout page.
field.usage: Chooses the layout of the PayPal Credit smart button shown on the checkout page. Applies only when the checkout-page button is customized with the credit label. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Installment period shown on the PayPal button for Mexico on the checkout page.
field.usage: Sets the Mexico installment period presented on the checkout-page PayPal smart button, from PayPal's available periods. Applies only when button customization is enabled and the button label is set to the installment option. Can be set per website or store view.
