field.usage: The port used for outgoing SMTP. It must match the port your mail server actually listens on, or mail silently fails to send. Accepts 0–65535 per the native note. Website/store scoped, so stores can use different mail servers.

field.summary: The Return-Path (bounce) address used for outbound email.
field.usage: The address that receives bounce notifications for outbound mail. Applies only when Set Return-Path is set to Specified. Must be a valid email. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether to set the email Return-Path header, and whether to use a specified address.
field.usage: Controls the Return-Path (bounce) address on outbound mail: No, Yes (use the sender address), or Specified (use the Return-Path Email below). Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The encryption used when connecting to the SMTP server.
field.usage: The connection security for SMTP: None, SSL, or TLS. Applies only when Transport is set to SMTP. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: How outbound mail is sent — via Sendmail or an SMTP server.
field.usage: Selects the mail transport: Sendmail (the local MTA) or SMTP (an external mail server). Choosing SMTP enables the related Auth and SSL settings. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The account name used to authenticate to your SMTP server for outgoing mail; blank means no SMTP login.
field.usage: The username Magento uses to log in to the SMTP server when sending mail. Applies only when the mail transport is SMTP. Leave blank only if the server accepts unauthenticated relay. Set per website or store view so each can send through a different mail account.

field.summary: How aggressively the browser preloads likely next pages; higher is faster but wastes more.
field.usage: Controls how eagerly the browser speculatively loads probable next pages. Applies only when speculative loading is enabled. As the native note says, higher eagerness loads pages sooner but may fetch ones never visited, adding server load and bandwidth. Can differ per scope.

field.summary: Yes uses the browser Speculation Rules API to prefetch/prerender likely next pages for faster navigation; adds speculative server load.
field.usage: When Yes, Magento emits Speculation Rules so supporting browsers prefetch or prerender pages before a link is clicked, making navigation feel faster (native note). The trade-off is extra load from speculative requests, and only modern browsers honour it. Can differ per website/store view.

field.summary: File extensions excluded from speculative prefetch/prerender; applies only when speculative loading is on.
field.usage: A comma-separated list of file extensions whose URLs are excluded from speculative prefetching/prerendering. Applies only when speculative loading is enabled, and is scoped per store view. Use it to keep downloads or heavy endpoints from being fetched ahead of a click.

field.summary: URL patterns (one per line) kept out of speculative prefetch/prerender, e.g. logout or cart actions.
field.usage: URLs matching these patterns (one per line) are excluded from speculative prefetch and prerender. Use it for logout, add-to-cart or anything with side effects you don't want triggered before the shopper clicks. Applies only when speculative loading is enabled.

field.summary: CSS selectors (one per line) whose links are excluded from speculative prerender/prefetch; applies only when speculative loading is on. Per website/store.
field.usage: Links matching these CSS selectors (one per line) are left out of speculative prerendering/prefetching. Use it to stop prefetching one-shot or state-changing links (logout, add-to-cart, delete) that could fire unintended actions. Applies only when speculative loading is enabled. Per website/store.

field.summary: Picks how aggressively browsers preload next pages; prerender is fastest but can skew analytics.
field.usage: Chooses the speculative-loading strategy browsers use to fetch likely next pages. Prerender is fastest but runs page JS before the page is opened, which can distort analytics unless accounted for. Applies only when speculative loading is enabled. Can differ per website/store.

field.summary: Yes resizes images in the browser before upload, cutting upload size and server load.
field.usage: When Yes, images are resized via JavaScript in the browser before being uploaded, reducing upload size, transfer time and server-side processing. It relies on client-side JS, so the browser does the work before the file is sent.

field.summary: JPEG compression (1-100) for resized images; higher is sharper but larger. Cached images keep old quality until regenerated.
field.usage: Compression quality applied when Magento resizes or generates JPEGs. Higher values look sharper but produce larger files and slower loads. It affects images generated after the change; already-cached images keep their old quality until the image cache is flushed and regenerated.

field.summary: Caps uploaded image height, scaling taller images down; active only when upload resize is on.
field.usage: Uploaded images taller than this are scaled down on upload, which lowers stored file size and keeps media dimensions consistent. Takes effect only when resize-on-upload is enabled.

field.summary: Caps the width of uploaded images; wider images are scaled down on upload.
field.usage: Maximum pixel width for newly uploaded images. Applies only when image resize on upload is enabled. Oversized uploads are scaled down to save storage and bandwidth; images already stored are not affected.

field.summary: Adds animated transitions between same-domain page loads.
field.usage: When enabled, animates transitions between pages loaded on the same domain for a smoother, app-like feel. Relies on browser support and degrades gracefully where absent. Can differ per website/store view.

field.summary: Whether to enable animated View Transitions in the Admin panel.
field.usage: When Yes, the browser View Transitions API is used to animate navigation within the Admin panel. Set to No to disable the effect.

field.summary: Yes animates back/forward navigation but may forgo the faster Back/Forward Cache restore.
field.usage: Yes animates back/forward navigation with view transitions, but doing so can bypass the browser's Back/Forward Cache that would otherwise restore the page instantly. No keeps that faster cached restore without the animation. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: How tax is rounded — per unit, per row, or on the total.
field.usage: The rounding method for tax: Unit Price (round each item), Row Total (round each line), or Total (round the order total). Affects cent-level differences on multi-item orders.

field.summary: Whether tax is applied before or after discounts.
field.usage: Chooses whether customer tax is calculated on the price Before Discount or After Discount — this changes the taxable base when promotions apply.

field.summary: Whether tax uses the custom price or the original price.
field.usage: Applies tax on the Custom price if available, or always on the Original price, for items with a special/custom price.

field.summary: Which address tax is calculated from.
field.usage: Whether tax is based on the Shipping Address, the Billing Address, or the store's Shipping Origin.

field.summary: Yes keeps tax-inclusive catalog prices identical across regions, absorbing differing tax rates into margin.
field.usage: When catalog prices include tax, setting Yes fixes the displayed price regardless of the customer's tax rate (per the note) — the advertised figure stays constant across regions and the differing tax is absorbed into your margin rather than changing the price. Only meaningful with tax-inclusive pricing. Set per website.

field.summary: Whether discounts apply to prices including or excluding tax; changes the taxable base.
field.usage: Chooses whether cart discounts are calculated on prices including or excluding tax, which shifts the taxable base. As the native note warns, applying the discount on tax-included prices requires Catalog Prices set to Including Tax. Saving flags a tax-configuration notice; website scoped.

field.summary: Whether catalog prices entered in admin already include tax; can differ per website.
field.usage: Tells the tax engine whether catalog prices entered in the admin are tax-inclusive, as the field note says. It changes whether tax is extracted from the entered price or added on top, so switching it shifts the effective shelf prices. Scoped to website.

field.summary: Declares whether entered/gateway shipping amounts already include tax; getting it wrong double-counts or omits shipping tax. Per website.
field.usage: Tells Magento whether shipping amounts (entered in admin or returned by carriers) already contain tax. If this is set wrong, shipping tax is either double-counted or dropped. Changing it alters how the shipping tax base is computed on new calculations. Scoped per website.

field.summary: Whether the cart breaks tax down by rate instead of a single line.
field.usage: When Yes, the cart shows a full tax summary (each tax rate itemised) rather than one combined tax line.

field.summary: Whether the cart also shows the order total without tax.
field.usage: When Yes, the cart additionally shows the grand total excluding tax alongside the taxed total.

field.summary: Whether cart item prices show including tax, excluding tax, or both.
field.usage: Price display for items in the shopping cart: Excluding Tax, Including Tax, or Including and Excluding Tax.

field.summary: Whether the cart shipping amount shows including tax, excluding tax, or both.
field.usage: Shipping-amount display in the cart: Excluding Tax, Including Tax, or Including and Excluding Tax.

field.summary: Whether the cart subtotal shows including tax, excluding tax, or both.
field.usage: Subtotal display in the cart: Excluding Tax, Including Tax, or Including and Excluding Tax.

field.summary: Whether a zero-value tax line is shown in the cart.
field.usage: When Yes, a tax line is shown even when the tax amount is zero; when No, it is hidden.

field.summary: The tax class assigned to a customer group when none is set.
field.usage: The default customer tax class, used together with the product tax class to resolve the applicable tax rate.

field.summary: The tax class assigned to a new product when none is set.
field.usage: The default product tax class used for products that don't specify one, determining which tax rates apply to them.

field.summary: The tax class applied to shipping charges.
field.usage: Which product tax class shipping is taxed under. Pick the class whose rates should apply to the shipping amount (or a 'None' class to leave shipping untaxed).

field.summary: Default country used to estimate tax before a customer address is known.
field.usage: The fallback destination country for tax estimation (e.g. catalog prices) until the customer provides an address.

field.summary: Default post code used to estimate tax before a customer address is known.
field.usage: The fallback destination post code for tax estimation. Use * to match any post code within the default region.

field.summary: Default state/region used to estimate tax before a customer address is known.
field.usage: The fallback destination state/region for tax estimation, paired with the Default Country.

field.summary: Whether shipping prices show including tax, excluding tax, or both.
field.usage: How shipping amounts are displayed in the catalog/estimates: Excluding Tax, Including Tax, or Including and Excluding Tax.

field.summary: Whether catalog prices show including tax, excluding tax, or both.
field.usage: How product prices appear in the catalog: Excluding Tax, Including Tax, or Including and Excluding Tax.

field.summary: Whether sales documents break tax down by rate instead of a single line.
field.usage: When Yes, sales documents show a full tax summary (each rate itemised) rather than one combined tax line.

field.summary: Whether sales documents also show the order total without tax.
field.usage: When Yes, orders, invoices and credit memos additionally show the grand total excluding tax.

field.summary: Whether prices on orders, invoices and credit memos show including tax, excluding tax, or both.
field.usage: Price display on sales documents (orders, invoices, credit memos): Excluding Tax, Including Tax, or Including and Excluding Tax.

field.summary: Whether the shipping amount on sales documents shows including tax, excluding tax, or both.
field.usage: Shipping-amount display on orders, invoices and credit memos: Excluding Tax, Including Tax, or Including and Excluding Tax.

field.summary: Whether the subtotal on sales documents shows including tax, excluding tax, or both.
field.usage: Subtotal display on orders, invoices and credit memos: Excluding Tax, Including Tax, or Including and Excluding Tax.

field.summary: Whether a zero-value tax line is shown on sales documents.
field.usage: When Yes, a tax line is shown on orders, invoices and credit memos even when the tax amount is zero.

field.summary: Whether tax is also applied on top of the Fixed Product Tax amount.
field.usage: When Yes, regular tax is calculated on the FPT amount as well as on the product price. Applies only when Enable FPT is Yes. Can differ per website.

field.summary: How Fixed Product Tax amounts are shown on the product view page.
field.usage: Controls the way FPT amounts are displayed on the product detail page. Applies only when Enable FPT is Yes. Can differ per website.

field.summary: How Fixed Product Tax amounts are shown in emails.
field.usage: Controls the way FPT amounts are displayed in transactional emails. Applies only when Enable FPT is Yes. Can differ per website.

field.summary: How Fixed Product Tax amounts are shown in product lists.
field.usage: Controls the way FPT amounts appear in category and other product lists (for example shown separately or rolled into the price). Applies only when Enable FPT is Yes. Can differ per website.

field.summary: How Fixed Product Tax amounts are shown in sales documents.
field.usage: Controls the way FPT amounts are displayed in sales areas such as the cart, orders and invoices. Applies only when Enable FPT is Yes. Can differ per website.

field.summary: Turns Fixed Product Tax (FPT) calculation on or off.
field.usage: When set to Yes, Fixed Product Tax (FPT) is calculated and applied to products that carry an FPT attribute. Can be set per website, so FPT can be active on one website and off on another.

field.summary: Whether the Fixed Product Tax is included in the order subtotal.
field.usage: When Yes, FPT is added into the order subtotal rather than shown as a separate amount. Applies only when Enable FPT is Yes. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The CardinalCommerce API Identifier used to authenticate 3-D Secure requests.
field.usage: The API Identifier credential issued by CardinalCommerce. Stored encrypted. Applies only when the integration is enabled. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The CardinalCommerce API key used to authenticate 3-D Secure requests.
field.usage: The API key credential issued by CardinalCommerce. Stored encrypted. Applies only when the integration is enabled. Can differ per website.

field.summary: Whether CardinalCommerce request and response details are written to the debug log.
field.usage: When Yes, CardinalCommerce communication is logged for troubleshooting. Applies only when the integration is enabled. Can differ per website.

field.summary: Whether CardinalCommerce 3-D Secure requests use the sandbox or production environment.
field.usage: Selects the CardinalCommerce target: Sandbox for testing or Production for live transactions. Applies only when the CardinalCommerce integration is enabled. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The CardinalCommerce Org Unit ID used to authenticate 3-D Secure requests.
field.usage: The Org Unit ID credential issued by CardinalCommerce for the Cardinal Cruise API. Stored encrypted. Applies only when the integration is enabled. Can differ per website.

field.summary: The 'From' email address for the Custom Email 1 store identity.
field.usage: The sender email address used when the Custom Email 1 identity is selected as the sender of a transactional email. Must be a valid email. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The 'From' display name for the Custom Email 1 store identity.
field.usage: The sender name shown on emails sent from the Custom Email 1 identity. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The 'From' email address for the Custom Email 2 store identity.
field.usage: The sender email address used when the Custom Email 2 identity is selected as the sender of a transactional email. Must be a valid email. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The 'From' display name for the Custom Email 2 store identity.
field.usage: The sender name shown on emails sent from the Custom Email 2 identity. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The 'From' email address for the General Contact store identity.
field.usage: The sender email address for the General Contact identity, the default sender for many store notifications. Must be a valid email. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The 'From' display name for the General Contact store identity.
field.usage: The sender name shown on emails sent from the General Contact identity. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The 'From' email address for the Sales Representative store identity.
field.usage: The sender email address for the Sales Representative identity, used as the sender of sales-related emails. Must be a valid email. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The 'From' display name for the Sales Representative store identity.
field.usage: The sender name shown on emails sent from the Sales Representative identity. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The 'From' email address for the Customer Support store identity.
field.usage: The sender email address for the Customer Support identity, used as the sender of support-related emails. Must be a valid email. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The 'From' display name for the Customer Support store identity.
field.usage: The sender name shown on emails sent from the Customer Support identity. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: The API key of your Authy account, used for Authy two-factor authentication; stored encrypted.
field.usage: The Authy API key that this store uses to send and verify Authy two-factor challenges. It is stored encrypted. Obtain it from your Authy/Twilio account.

field.summary: The approval message shown to users in Authy OneTouch push requests.
field.usage: The text displayed in the Authy OneTouch approval prompt that users receive when signing in. Use it to identify the request.

field.summary: The API hostname of your Duo Security account.
field.usage: The Duo API hostname (for example the api-….duosecurity.com host from your Duo admin panel) that this store contacts for the Duo Universal Prompt.

field.summary: The Client ID of your Duo Security application, used for the Duo Universal Prompt.
field.usage: Identifies the Duo Security application that authenticates admin sign-ins via the Duo Universal Prompt. Obtain it from your Duo admin panel and enter it here.

field.summary: The Client Secret of your Duo Security application; stored encrypted.
field.usage: The secret paired with the Duo Client Id for the Duo Universal Prompt. It is stored encrypted. Obtain it from your Duo admin panel.

field.summary: The integration key of your Duo Security application.
field.usage: The integration key issued for the Duo application used by the Duo Universal Prompt. Obtain it from your Duo admin panel.

field.summary: The secret key of your Duo Security application; stored encrypted.
field.usage: The secret key paired with the Duo Integration Key. It is stored encrypted. Obtain it from your Duo admin panel.

field.summary: How long a user is locked out after hitting the failed-2FA threshold; longer deters brute-force attempts.
field.usage: Time, in seconds, a user stays locked out once they reach the failed two-factor-attempt threshold. Longer periods deter brute-forcing codes; shorter ones reduce lockout frustration. Must be between 120 and 1800 (30 minutes).

field.summary: Which 2FA methods admin users are allowed to use at login.
field.usage: Restricts the two-factor authentication methods admin users may use when signing in. Selecting several providers lets each admin choose among them; narrowing to one enforces that method for everyone. Default scope — it applies to all admins.

field.summary: How many 2FA attempts are allowed before a temporary lockout; lower resists code-guessing but risks locking out admins who mistype.
field.usage: Sets how many times an admin can attempt the two-factor step before a temporary lockout (native note). Lower values harden against code-guessing; set it too low and legitimate admins who mistype get locked out. Global setting (default scope).

field.summary: Custom URL for the 2FA setup link in Web API auth emails; must include the :tfat placeholder for the token.
field.usage: Overrides the default 2FA configuration link sent in Web API authentication emails, pointing it at a URL you choose (per the note). It must contain the :tfat placeholder marking where the token is injected, or the generated link won't work. Default scope.

field.summary: Clock-drift tolerance (seconds) for Google Authenticator OTPs; must be below the period.
field.usage: Seconds of clock-drift tolerance when validating Google Authenticator OTPs, and must stay below the OTP period (see the native example). A larger leeway accepts more server/device time skew but widens the window each code stays valid, a small security trade-off.

field.summary: WebAuthn domain for U2F key challenges via Web API; must match registration or auth fails.
field.usage: The WebAuthn relying-party domain used when issuing and verifying U2F security-key challenges over the Web API. It must match the domain where keys were registered or authentication fails; leave blank to use the store domain.

field.summary: Whether dynamically-defined attributes are exposed as fields on their entity types in the GraphQL schema.
field.usage: When Yes, dynamic (store-defined) attributes appear as typed fields on their entity in the GraphQL schema rather than only through generic containers. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: Warn visitors whose browser blocks cookies.
field.usage: When Yes, customers whose browser has cookies disabled are shown a notice, since the store needs cookies to work.

field.summary: Warn visitors whose browser has JavaScript off.
field.usage: When Yes, a notice is shown to customers with JavaScript disabled.

field.summary: Warn visitors whose browser blocks local storage.
field.usage: When Yes, a notice is shown to customers whose browser has local storage disabled.

field.summary: The domain cookies are set for.
field.usage: The domain used when setting cookies. Leave blank to use the current domain, or set it (e.g. .example.com) to share cookies across subdomains.

field.summary: Mark cookies as HTTP-only (recommended).
field.usage: When Yes, cookies cannot be read by JavaScript, which protects them from theft. Do not set to No — it weakens security.

field.summary: How long cookies live (seconds).
field.usage: The lifetime of session and other cookies, in seconds.

field.summary: The path cookies are scoped to.
field.usage: The URL path cookies apply to. Use / for the whole site, or a subpath to limit them.

field.summary: Enable cookie-consent restriction mode.
field.usage: When Yes, Cookie Restriction Mode asks visitors to consent before non-essential cookies are set, for privacy compliance.

field.summary: The CMS page used as the storefront home page.
field.usage: Which CMS page is shown at the store's root URL.

field.summary: The CMS page shown when cookies are disabled.
field.usage: Which CMS page is displayed to visitors whose browser blocks cookies.

field.summary: The CMS page shown for 404 (not found).
field.usage: Which CMS page is displayed when a requested URL doesn't exist.

field.summary: The default route loaded at the store root.
field.usage: The action path loaded at the store root (default cms), before the home page resolves.

field.summary: The default page layout for category pages.
field.usage: The column layout applied to category pages unless an individual category overrides it.

field.summary: The default page layout for CMS pages.
field.usage: The column layout applied to CMS pages unless an individual page overrides it.

field.summary: The default page layout for product pages.
field.usage: The column layout applied to product pages unless an individual product overrides it.

field.summary: The route that handles not-found URLs.
field.usage: The action path (for example cms/noroute/index) used when no route matches a request.

field.summary: Show breadcrumbs on CMS pages.
field.usage: When Yes, breadcrumb navigation is shown on CMS pages.

field.summary: The secure base URL used for links.
field.usage: The HTTPS base used when building links. May start with {{secure_base_url}} or {{unsecure_base_url}}.

field.summary: The secure base URL for media files.
field.usage: The HTTPS base for product and other media. Leave empty to derive it from the secure base URL.

field.summary: The secure base URL for static files.
field.usage: The HTTPS base for compiled static assets (CSS/JS). Leave empty to derive it from the secure base URL.

field.summary: The store's secure (HTTPS) base URL.
field.usage: The root HTTPS URL of the store. Specify a full URL or a placeholder such as {{base_url}}.

field.summary: Send the HSTS security header.
field.usage: When Yes, the store sends HTTP Strict Transport Security, telling browsers to always use HTTPS. Make sure HTTPS works everywhere first.

field.summary: Upgrade insecure requests to HTTPS.
field.usage: When Yes, the store asks browsers to automatically load any HTTP resources over HTTPS instead.

field.summary: Header used to detect SSL termination upstream.
field.usage: The request header a load balancer or proxy sets to signal that SSL was terminated before Magento (for example X-Forwarded-Proto).

field.summary: Serve the admin over HTTPS.
field.usage: When Yes, secure (HTTPS) URLs are used in the admin.

field.summary: Serve the storefront over HTTPS.
field.usage: When Yes, secure (HTTPS) URLs are used on the storefront.

field.summary: Use clean URLs without index.php.
field.usage: When Yes, server rewrites remove index.php from URLs. Requires the web server to support URL rewrites.

field.summary: Validate the session against the User-Agent.
field.usage: When Yes, a session is tied to the browser's User-Agent, adding a check against session hijacking.

field.summary: Validate the session against the Via header.
field.usage: When Yes, the Via header is included in session validation. May cause problems behind some proxies.

field.summary: Validate the session against X-Forwarded-For.
field.usage: When Yes, the X-Forwarded-For header is included in session validation. May cause problems behind some proxies or CDNs.

field.summary: Validate the session against the client IP.
field.usage: When Yes, a session is tied to the client's IP address. May break for users whose IP changes mid-session.

field.summary: The base URL used for links.
field.usage: The base used when building links. May start with {{unsecure_base_url}}.

field.summary: The base URL for media files.
field.usage: The base for product and other media. Leave empty to derive it from the base URL.

field.summary: The base URL for static files.
field.usage: The base for compiled static assets (CSS/JS). Leave empty to derive it from the base URL.

field.summary: The store's base (HTTP) URL.
field.usage: The root URL of the store. Specify a full URL or a placeholder such as {{base_url}}.

field.summary: How catalog image URLs are formed.
field.usage: Whether product image variants are served via query parameters (CDN-friendly) or as uniquely hashed files (legacy mode).

field.summary: Redirect unrecognized hosts to the base URL.
field.usage: Whether requests to a non-base host are redirected to the configured base URL, and with which redirect code.

field.summary: Put the store code in URLs.
field.usage: When Yes, the store code is added to URLs (for example /en/). Warning: can cause issues in some setups.

field.summary: Whether to disable PHP session handling for GraphQL requests.
field.usage: When Yes, GraphQL requests are served without starting a PHP session, which can improve performance for stateless API traffic.

field.summary: Whether to enforce a maximum number of field aliases in a GraphQL query.
field.usage: When Yes, GraphQL queries using more than the allowed number of aliases are rejected, limiting a known request-amplification technique. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether to enforce configured limits on GraphQL query input size.
field.usage: When Yes, the configured GraphQL input limits are enforced, rejecting queries that exceed them. A safeguard against overly large or abusive queries. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: Caps aliases per GraphQL request to curb abuse; set too low and legitimate queries fail.
field.usage: Limits how many aliases a single GraphQL request may use, a guard against resource-exhaustion attacks. Applies only when the alias limit is enabled. Set it too low and complex but legitimate queries are rejected. Website/store scoped.

field.summary: Caps pageSize on GraphQL queries to block expensive requests; applies only when input limits are on. Too low breaks large listings.
field.usage: Upper bound on how many items a single paginated GraphQL query may request, protecting the server from oversized or expensive calls. Applies only when GraphQL input limits are enabled; setting it below what the storefront asks for will make those queries fail. Per website/store.

field.summary: Max characters allowed in a GraphQL request; longer queries are rejected. Applies only when the length limit is on.
field.usage: The maximum number of characters a GraphQL query string may contain; larger requests are rejected. It guards against oversized or abusive queries. Applies only when the GraphQL query-length limit is enabled. Set per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether to enforce a maximum character length for GraphQL queries.
field.usage: When Yes, GraphQL queries longer than the allowed character count are rejected. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: Lifetime in minutes of an admin API JWT before it must be reissued.
field.usage: How long, in minutes, an admin user's JWT stays valid for API calls. Shorter lifetimes limit the damage of a leaked token but force more frequent re-authentication; longer ones are more convenient but riskier. Default scope only.

field.summary: Lifetime, in minutes, of customer JWT access tokens; shorter is more secure but forces more frequent re-authentication.
field.usage: How long, in minutes, a customer's JWT access token stays valid. A shorter lifetime limits the damage from a stolen token but makes customers and clients re-authenticate more often; a longer one is more convenient but riskier.

field.summary: Content-encryption algorithm used when API tokens are issued as encrypted JWEs.
field.usage: Selects the algorithm that encrypts the payload of JWT tokens. As the field note says, it takes effect when a JWE (encrypted) algorithm is in use rather than a plain signed token, keeping the token contents opaque to the client.

field.summary: Algorithm for auth JWTs; signing gives a readable JWS, encryption a confidential JWE.
field.usage: The algorithm used to sign or encrypt authentication JWTs. A signing algorithm produces a JWS (tamper-evident but readable); an encryption algorithm produces a JWE (also confidential). It must match what your API clients expect or tokens are rejected.

field.summary: Character set declared on SOAP API responses; empty uses UTF-8. Change only if a client needs another encoding.
field.usage: The character set declared on SOAP Web API responses; left empty, UTF-8 is used (per the note). Change it only when a consuming client requires a different encoding, since UTF-8 is the safe default for most integrations. Set per website or store view.

field.summary: Maximum items allowed in an array property of a Web API request, blocking oversized payloads; applies only when input limiting is on.
field.usage: Caps how many elements an array property may contain in a Web API request body, guarding against oversized or abusive payloads (native note). Applies only when Web API input limits are enabled (depends). Can differ per website/store view.

field.summary: Default page size for API search results when the client doesn't specify one.
field.usage: Number of records returned per page for REST/GraphQL search results when the request omits a page size. Larger values mean fewer round-trips but heavier responses and more memory per call. Can differ per website/store view.

field.summary: Whether Web API requests enforce limits on the size of input arrays and collections.
field.usage: When Yes, the Web API enforces input limits, such as the maximum number of items accepted in a request, rejecting oversized payloads to protect the store. Configured under Magento Web API → Web Api Input Limits.

field.summary: Caps items per page on API searches to block oversized, expensive requests; only when input limits are on.
field.usage: Maximum number of items allowed in a paginated API search result, preventing oversized and resource-heavy requests. Enforced only when API input limits are enabled. Can differ per website/store.

field.summary: Permits anonymous access to normally-protected CMS, Catalog and Store APIs; a security risk.
field.usage: When Yes, allows unauthenticated access to API resources that are otherwise protected, limited to CMS, Catalog and Store APIs per the native note. It exposes data without auth, so review the risk with developers before enabling. Default scope.

field.summary: Which store email identity wish list sharing emails are sent from.
field.usage: Selects the sender identity used when a customer shares a wish list by email — one of the Store Email Addresses identities (General Contact, Sales Representative, Customer Support, Custom 1/2). Can differ per store view.

field.summary: Template for the shared wish-list email; Default follows theme fallback.
field.usage: The template for the email sent when a customer shares their wish list. Default follows theme fallback; a custom template overrides it. Can differ per website or store view.

field.summary: Caps how many recipients a single wishlist-share email can have; can differ per store view.
field.usage: The maximum number of recipient addresses allowed when sharing a wish list by email. As the field note says, the default is 10 and the ceiling is 10000. Scoped to website/store, so each store view can set its own limit.

field.summary: Max characters in the personal message when a wishlist is shared (255 by default, up to 10000); raising it allows longer notes. Per website/store.
field.usage: Caps the length of the personal message a customer can add when sharing a wish list, 255 by default and up to 10000. Raising it permits longer notes at some added risk of abuse/spam. Settable per website/store.

field.summary: Turns the storefront wish list feature on or off.
field.usage: When Yes, customers can add products to a wish list; No disables the feature. Can be set per website or store view.

field.summary: Whether the wish list block appears in the storefront sidebar.
field.usage: When Yes, a wish list block is shown in the storefront sidebar. Applies only when Enabled (wish list) is set to Yes. Can differ per store view.

field.summary: What the My Wish List link summary displays for its contents.
field.usage: Controls how the My Wish List link summarises the list's contents (such as item count versus quantity). Can differ per website.
